commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Overlap the mHC gate projection with attention and FFN
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, each DeepSeek V4.1 mHC seam ran the whole fused AITER kernel pair on the default stream before the next sublayer could start. That pair is the post block, the gate projection, Sinkhorn, and the collapse with RMSNorm. This PR moves the gate projection onto a side stream inside FULL HIP graphs, so it overlaps with the following attention or FFN. The default stream now only runs the post block plus the RMSNorm'd collapse, in one new Triton kernel. This is the ROCm counterpart of the CUDA overlap in [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603).

## Claims

- Output throughput is up 0.3% to 5.4% end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, EP, FP8 KV, MI355X, at every concurrency from 1 to 128 at TP2, TP4 and TP8.
- The new residual and the gates (post, comb, next pre) are bit-identical to the fused AITER seam. The layer input is bit-identical up to 16 tokens and within one bf16 ulp above that.
- No change outside FULL-graph decode with at most 128 tokens. Prefill, piecewise graphs, eager mode, CUDA and DSpark draft layers keep the current path.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, HIP-graph replay time per seam. "Fused" is `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` (main + reduce kernels). "Input kernel" is the new `mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton`, the only part left on the default stream. "Gates" is the side-stream work.


| tokens | fused (µs) | input kernel (µs) | gates on side stream (µs) |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1      | 9.91       | 4.15              | 8.48                      |
| 4      | 10.24      | 4.26              | 9.01                      |
| 16     | 10.41      | 4.37              | 9.17                      |


The default-stream seam goes from about 10 µs to about 4.3 µs. That is roughly 0.5 ms per decode step across the 86 seams that take the overlap (43 layers × 2).

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, TP4, EP, FP8 KV, 12 sweep points. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | Δ     | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | --------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------- | ------------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.08      | 7.70         | -4.8% | 466.71     | 488.68        | +4.7% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.80      | 9.46         | -3.5% | 773.17     | 799.60        | +3.4% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.84     | 11.50        | -2.9% | 1262.50    | 1300.66       | +3.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.12     | 15.69        | -2.7% | 1786.03    | 1833.31       | +2.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.14     | 22.90        | -1.1% | 2516.82    | 2539.97       | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.31     | 34.51        | -2.3% | 3161.18    | 3225.27       | +2.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 58.27     | 57.96        | -0.5% | 3795.31    | 3815.37       | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 13.80     | 13.47        | -2.4% | 227.83     | 233.61        | +2.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 39.88     | 39.98        | +0.2% | 337.21     | 338.35        | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 138.79    | 136.17       | -1.9% | 388.60     | 394.46        | +1.5% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.85     | 16.53        | -1.9% | 185.12     | 187.66        | +1.4% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 54.22     | 53.73        | -0.9% | 247.55     | 250.08        | +1.0% |


The mean is -2.05% TPOT and +2.00% throughput. Throughput is higher at all 12 points and TPOT lower at 11; the exception is 60000 / 600 at concurrency 16, at +0.2%. Median TPOT gives -2.14%, also 11 of 12, so the whole distribution moves rather than a tail.

**TP2, TP4 and TP8 at concurrency 1 to 128.** Random 2048 in / 256 out, same build for both arms on one node, overlap on against `MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS=0`. The overlap arm ran with a limit of 512, which at these concurrencies covers the same decode steps as 128. TP2 and TP8 had a warm-up pass and TP4 did not. These sweeps predate the switch to the global aux stream and events. Change in output throughput:

| concurrency | TP2   | TP4   | TP8   |
| ----------- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1           | +5.4% | +5.2% | +5.4% |
| 2           | +5.0% | +5.4% | +4.9% |
| 4           | +4.5% | +4.7% | +4.0% |
| 8           | +3.4% | +3.7% | +3.6% |
| 16          | +3.0% | +3.2% | +4.2% |
| 24          | +2.3% | +3.9% | +3.7% |
| 32          | +1.9% | +2.9% | +2.6% |
| 48          | +2.2% | +2.8% | +3.7% |
| 64          | +1.3% | +2.9% | +2.4% |
| 96          | +0.8% | +2.0% | +0.3% |
| 128         | +1.4% | +1.7% | +1.4% |

Every point improves. The gain shrinks from about +5% at concurrency 1 to +0.3–2% at 96–128, where it is within about 1% run-to-run noise.

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, full test split, `num_concurrent=32`:


| run     | flexible-extract | strict-match    |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| default | 0.9227 ± 0.0074  | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |
| this PR | 0.9234 ± 0.0073  | 0.9234 ± 0.0073 |


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rocm
```

All pass on MI355X. `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mhc_overlap_matches_fused_seam` is new and runs at 1, 2, 7, 16, 64 and 128 tokens. After joining the side stream, it compares every output with `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` (the fused AITER seam):

- the residual and gates must match exactly;
- the layer input must match within one bf16 ulp, and it must already be usable before the join;
- the same checks are repeated across three HIP-graph replays with changing inputs.

CI runs it in `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels`.

## Details

**Why the split is exact.** In AITER's fused seam (`_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel`), the post-mix is rounded to bf16 once, and that rounded `R'` feeds the projection, the square sums and the collapse. This PR splits the seam in two:

- The new kernel recomputes `R'` with the same expression order, so it is bit-identical, then collapses it with the carried pre-mix and applies the RMSNorm.
- The side stream runs AITER's own fused kernel on `R'` without the post (`HAS_POST=False`). Its gates are therefore the same numbers.

Only the RMSNorm's row sum differs. The new kernel holds a token's row in registers and sums it in one pass, while AITER reduces it across split-K programs, so the order changes. That is exact at decode sizes, and within one ulp otherwise.

**Gating.** The overlap runs only inside FULL HIP-graph capture, not in piecewise graphs, with `0 < tokens <= MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (128). Fork and join then become graph edges; `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` keeps its aux streams to captured graphs for the same reason. It also requires AITER's fused delayed seam (`HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM`), `hc_mult == 4`, and no ubatching. The 128-token limit is the largest tested point. The gain was still positive there but shrinking (above), and the overlap was not measured beyond it, although FULL graphs go up to 512 tokens.

**Seams.** The overlap applies to every FFN seam and to the attention seam of every layer after the first. Layer 0's broadcast seam and Engram seams already take a different path and keep it. The gate stream is joined after attention and at the end of each layer, which is where the gates are next read. The stream is separate from the attention aux streams, as on CUDA. `record_stream` keeps the side stream's inputs and the main stream's gate outputs alive across the fork. No host synchronization is added.

**Limitations.**

- **Tuning:** the token limit was tuned on MI355X TP2, TP4 and TP8.



### Existing PRs

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for mHC overlap, coefficient and side-stream work on ROCm. None moves the mHC seam off the default stream on ROCm.

- [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603) (merged) is the CUDA version. It needs SM100 and DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, and stops at 16 tokens. This PR follows its structure, gating and join points.
- [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) (merged) adds an attention-side aux stream for DeepSeek-V4 HCA layers. It keeps the mHC seam serial on the default stream, which is what this PR changes.
- [#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) (merged) introduced the fused AITER delayed seam that this PR splits.


---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Sync cluster before DSMEM stores in ll_bf16 split-K router GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The `ll_bf16` split-K router GEMM (#42562, M >= 8) stores partials into peer CTAs' shared memory (`st.shared::cluster`) before any cluster barrier. If a peer CTA hasn't started yet, the GPU raises Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`, which surfaces as `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`.

Fix: all threads `cluster_arrive_relaxed()` after pipeline init. DMA warps `cluster_wait()` after committing stage 0, and MMA warps wait at the start of their branch. So every peer is resident before the epilogue's `st.shared::cluster`, and the wait stays out of the PDL prologue (split suggested by @LopezCastroRoberto).

## Reproduction

This uses @Skyseaee's single-GPU harness ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61463#issuecomment-6210051133)). It runs the router GEMM in a CUDA graph, concurrent with non-cluster copy kernels that write to mapped pinned host memory:
```bash
nvcc -O3 -shared -Xcompiler -fPIC -arch=sm_103a copy.cu -o libhostcopy.so
python -u router_probe.py --tag <tag> --mode direct --seconds 120
```

| B300, fresh process per run | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`a12e122206`) | `unspecified launch failure` in the first batch, 4/4 runs |
| this PR (`ac5c06ee4b`) | 120 s clean, 4,912,896 router calls, outputs correct |

The harness does not trigger the fault on H200. In serving, the same Xid hit GLM-5.3 HiSparse P/D decode (2x 8xH200, TP4) within minutes. The first revision of this fix (arrive+wait at kernel start) ran 6/6 passes clean there; the current revision has not been run in serving.

No regression test: the race depends on hardware CTA scheduling, so it can't be made deterministic. `test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` covers numerics only.

## Test results

All on `ac5c06ee4b`.

`pytest tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py`: 144 passed on B300 and on H200.

Latency is µs per call: the median of 30 replays of a CUDA graph holding 200 back-to-back PDL `ll_bf16_gemm` calls, N=256.

| GPU, K | M=8 / 12 / 16, `main` | M=8 / 12 / 16, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| B300, 6144 | 2.45 / 2.74 / 2.71 | 2.47 / 2.81 / 2.77 |
| B300, 7168 | 2.78 / 2.79 / 2.76 | 2.80 / 2.80 / 2.76 |
| B300, 4096 | 2.59 / 2.46 / 2.47 | 2.61 / 2.47 / 2.47 |
| H200, 6144 | 2.62 / 2.68 / 2.72 | 2.66 / 2.72 / 2.75 |
| H200, 7168 | 2.79 / 2.78 / 2.85 | 2.84 / 2.82 / 2.88 |
| H200, 4096 | 2.40 / 2.61 / 3.00 | 2.44 / 2.66 / 2.94 |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Restore the Torch Stable ABI Audit mirror with a locked audit tool
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Restores the `(MI300) Torch Stable ABI Audit` mirror that #63608 disabled, by locking `torch-abi-audit` in the ROCm test requirements instead of installing it at job runtime.

## Claims

- Closes the only AMD parity gap in the Torch ABI area, 0% to 100%.
- Drops the runtime `uv pip install` that got the job disabled.

## Validation

`.buildkite/check-torch-abi.py` on a gfx950 build:

```
>>> Auditing vLLM extension modules for PyTorch stable ABI compliance
Torch stable ABI check passed.
```

## Details

`torch-abi-audit` is in `requirements/test/cuda.in` but was missing on the ROCm side, so the mirror added in #50519 had to fetch it during the job. Declaring it in `requirements/test/rocm.in` removes that, which is the condition #63608 asked for.

Pinned to `0.0.1` to match the cuda and cpu locks. The first CI run rebuilds the runtime and test-deps images, since `requirements/test/rocm.txt` feeds their key; the stack key is untouched.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Skip the GPU coredump in MonoKernel fault-injection tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Turns off the GPU coredump for the two tests in the `:amd: (MI355) MiniMax M3 MonoKernel` group that inject a rank fault on purpose. They spend most of their time writing a dump nobody reads.

## Claims

- The two tests are 74% of the group's runtime (782.52s of 1058.67s in build 96864).
- No coverage change: same tests, same assertions, same count.
- Scope is those two tests only, because only they are written to crash.

## Details

The group is defined in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` (key `minimax-m3-monokernel-mi355`, `device: mi355_4`), and mirrored internally as `(MI355) MiniMax M3 Specialized Decode`.

Both tests arm `_arm_late_fault` and assert `EngineDeadError`, so the fault is expected. When a rank faults, `libhsa-runtime64` writes a file-based dump and the worker stays alive while writing. The executor never sees it die, so it waits out the full `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300). With the dump off the worker dies, its response queue closes, and `mq.dequeue` raises right away.

The same thing is already done on the NVIDIA side, by #61263, for a test that also crashes a kernel on purpose: `test_hisparse_expanded_hash_keeps_union_bound` in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` passes `CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION=0`. That one belongs to the `Attention` group's `(B200) V1 Attention` step. There was no ROCm equivalent anywhere in the repo.

The fixture is function-scoped and not `autouse`, so it covers only the two tests written to crash. Everything else in the group keeps the default behaviour.

## Validation

Two single-job runs of the step, one day apart, same two commands:

| Build | Branch | Step time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 99871 | main | 20m 44s |
| 99900 | this PR | **7m 45s** |

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Let cooperative_topk read the BF16 indexer logits
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`cooperative_topk` now also reads BF16 logits. On SM100 the DSA indexer then keeps the paged MQA logits in BF16
instead of upcasting them to FP32 before the decode top-k. Main already does this for `deep_select` and (since
#64138) `persistent`, but `auto` picks `cooperative` for up to 64 rows, which is every decode step in the runs
below (at most 16 requests x 4 tokens). From review, the top-k kernels themselves are also faster now, mostly
for BF16 (Details).

## Claims

- Decode top-k on B300, main (FP32 upcast + FP32 top-k) vs this PR (BF16 top-k): 22% to 57% faster at every
  point of rows {1, 4, 8, 16, 33, 64} x row length {16K, 64K, 128K, 256K, 1M} x k {512, 2048}. The BF16
  top-k alone is 8% to 38% faster than main's FP32 top-k. With FP32 logits (#64580's default) the top-k is up
  to 16% faster and at most 0.2% slower.
- `persistent_topk` with BF16 logits (#64138) is 24% to 31% faster on rows up to 32K, the single-CTA path it
  shares with `cooperative_topk`.
- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200: together with #62170 and #62171, decode time per turn
  drops 2.8%, 2.5%, 1.5% and 1.5% at concurrency 1, 4, 8 and 16 (main vs main: within 0.7%). This PR is
  about 1/3 of that. (Measured before the kernel changes from review.)
- No precision changes: DeepGEMM's SM100 logits kernels already return BF16 on main
  ([`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd/vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py#L597-L606)), and main only widens them
  ([`as_fp32_logits`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L304-L305)). BF16 widens to FP32
  exactly, so the top-k selects the same values.
- DCP, top-k backends that take only FP32, and BF16 rows that are not 16-byte aligned still upcast as before.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` on B300 (SM103), rebased onto main 602811546b: 870 passed, 44 skipped
  (main: 806 passed, 44 skipped). Each kernel commit also passes the file's cooperative and persistent tests.
  `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride` now runs FP32 and BF16 logits through every cluster size and
  both paths. `test_cooperative_topk_16bit_grid_overflow` (register and cluster paths) and
  `test_cooperative_topk_streaming_overflow` run the same BF16-grid values as FP32, which is what main passes today,
  and as BF16; both must select exactly the `torch.topk` values through #59645's overflow recovery.
  `test_cooperative_topk_overflow_nan` (#63118), `test_cooperative_topk_overflow_cluster_boundary` and
  `test_cooperative_topk_overflow_mixed_lengths` also run BF16 logits.
  `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` checks when `cooperative` takes BF16 logits, and
  `test_sparse_indexer_resolved_persistent_bf16` (#64138) now expects `auto`'s `cooperative` choice to take them
  too and checks that its selection is exact.
- Decode top-k, B300, `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph` median (L2 not flushed). Logits are `torch.randn`
  rounded to BF16, every row is full length, row stride = length. Main and this PR each ran twice in fresh
  processes, ordered main, PR, PR, main (same build twice: median 0.1%, max 3.3% apart). Every result selects
  exactly `torch.topk`'s values.

**k = 512**, µs, main (upcast + FP32 top-k) → this PR (BF16 top-k):

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

```python
"""cooperative_topk sweep for vllm#62172: rows x row length x k, timed with triton's do_bench_cudagraph.

usage: python coop_sweep.py TAG OUT_JSON  (from the vLLM tree to test, with its _C_stable_libtorch built)
       SWEEP_ONLY=fp32 times only the FP32 kernel, so both builds make the same allocations.
Logits are torch.randn rounded to BF16 (what DeepGEMM returns on SM100); every row has the full length and the
row stride equals the length. Timed per case (median us of CUDA-graph replays; L2 is not flushed):
  fp32          cooperative_topk on the FP32 widening (main's top-k kernel)
  upcast_fp32   as_fp32_logits(BF16) + cooperative_topk on FP32 (main's SM100 decode stage)
  bf16          cooperative_topk reading BF16 directly (this PR; None where the build rejects BF16)
Each result must select exactly torch.topk's values, with no repeated index. Run main, PR, PR, main in fresh
processes and compare the means of each build's two runs.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import torch
from triton.testing import do_bench_cudagraph

import vllm._custom_ops  # noqa: F401  (registers torch.ops._C)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer import as_fp32_logits

tag, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
ROWS = (1, 4, 8, 16, 33, 64)
LENGTHS = (16384, 65536, 131072, 262144, 1048576)
KS = (512, 2048)
ws = torch.empty(1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")


def bench(fn):
    return do_bench_cudagraph(fn, rep=100, return_mode="median") * 1000


def exact(logits32, out, k):
    sel = logits32.gather(1, out.long()).sort(1).values
    ref = logits32.topk(k, dim=1).values.sort(1).values
    uniq = all(out[r].unique().numel() == k for r in range(out.shape[0]))
    return bool(torch.equal(sel, ref)) and uniq


# Warm up (clocks, graph capture) on the first shape; the first timed case of a process reads high otherwise.
_x = torch.randn(ROWS[0], LENGTHS[0], device="cuda")
_l = torch.full((ROWS[0],), LENGTHS[0], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
_o = torch.empty(ROWS[0], KS[0], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
torch.cuda.synchronize()
bench(lambda: torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(_x, _l, _o, ws, KS[0], LENGTHS[0]))

results = []
for rows in ROWS:
    for length in LENGTHS:
        torch.manual_seed(rows * 7 + length)
        logits16 = torch.randn(rows, length, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
        logits32 = logits16.float()
        lengths = torch.full((rows,), length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        # do_bench_cudagraph runs on a side stream that does not wait for these writes.
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        for k in KS:
            r = dict(tag=tag, rows=rows, length=length, k=k)
            out = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

            def fp32():
                torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(logits32, lengths, out, ws, k, length)

            r["fp32"] = bench(fp32)
            r["fp32_exact"] = exact(logits32, out, k)
            if os.environ.get("SWEEP_ONLY") == "fp32":
                # Same allocations in every build: skip the BF16 variants.
                r["upcast_fp32"] = r["bf16"] = None
                r["upcast_fp32_exact"] = r["bf16_exact"] = True
                results.append(r)
                print(json.dumps(r), flush=True)
                continue

            def upcast_fp32():
                x = as_fp32_logits(logits16, lengths)
                torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(x, lengths, out, ws, k, length)

            r["upcast_fp32"] = bench(upcast_fp32)
            r["upcast_fp32_exact"] = exact(logits32, out, k)

            def bf16():
                torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(logits16, lengths, out, ws, k, length)

            try:
                bf16()
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
                r["bf16"] = bench(bf16)
                r["bf16_exact"] = exact(logits32, out, k)
            except RuntimeError:
                r["bf16"] = r["bf16_exact"] = None
            results.append(r)
            print(json.dumps(r), flush=True)
        del logits16, logits32
json.dump(results, open(out_path, "w"))
```

</details>

- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, main + #62170, #62171 and #62172 vs main (median per-turn change
  on the same turns, 95% CI; setup below):

  | KV cache tokens | +0.2% | +0.7% | +1.4% | 0 |
  | main vs main, decode | -0.1% | -0.7% | +0.3% | -0.3% |

- Target verify forward (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, B300, MTP verify shapes, spread < 0.1%), on top of #62170 and #62171 and before the kernel changes from
  review: -0.28% to -0.75% at 1, 3 and 7 requests, 25K and 94K context.
- Exactness: with real MTP verification on 32 GSM8K questions (greedy), the three changes together give the same

- MRCR (OpenAI, 8 needles, 594 samples), GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, TP4, greedy, thinking off; main vs main +

## Details

- `CooperativeTopKParams`, the TMA staging buffers and the histogram loads are templated on the input type.
- TMA units are 16 bytes (8 BF16 or 4 FP32 elements), so the stride and per-block alignment follow the element
  size.
- Scores are widened to FP32 when binned, so both input types use the same radix keys.
- #59645's exact overflow recovery in `cooperative_topk_overflow.cuh` reads scores through the widening helpers
  #64138 added (`to_float`, `load_score4`), so a BF16 row recovers exactly as its FP32 widening does.
- The extension dispatches on `logits.scalar_type()`.
- `SparseIndexerTopk.takes_bf16_logits` (from #64138) now also returns true for `cooperative`, explicit or as
  `auto`'s choice, when its constraints hold (at most 64 rows; contiguous, 16-byte-aligned rows).
- Candidate-block selection (DeepSeek-V4.1) keeps FP32 block scores for explicit `cooperative`, as main does for
  `auto` and `persistent`. On B300, BF16 and FP32 block scores select the same blocks, including rows where every
  block ties. I could not run that model here.

Kernel changes from review, each A/B'd on B300 against the step before it (same method as above):

| commit | change | effect |
|---|---|---|
| [d8a0039](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/d8a0039505edf7c8e1bdbc84b3010ec68c30f45d) | The tie refinement ORs the ties' keys against the first one and runs only the radix-256 rounds over bits they differ in: one for BF16 (keys end in 16 zero bits), usually three for FP32. FP32 keeps the four rounds in the single-CTA path, where the extra pass measured up to 0.9% slower even on rows that refine no ties | with the next row, rows 1 to 64 at 64K and 256K: BF16 -11% to -21%, FP32 -2% to -16% |
| [f45b4b4](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/f45b4b4e3cdb53314635213e4172cc340fd52068) | The BF16 hot loops read two staged scores per 32-bit load and bin both with one packed FP16 conversion and key flip. An exhaustive GPU check gives the same bins as the scalar path for all 2^32 inputs | (above) |
| [ff286db](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/ff286dbe970d1929f9ec4a97d2450c8f2def8d88) | BF16 keeps twice as many elements resident in the same shared memory | -18% to -20% where rows now fit a single pass (4x1M, 8x512K, 16x256K, 33x256K, 64x128K to 192K), unchanged elsewhere |
| [9970c5a](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172/commits/9970c5ac5b4e6664400890d11159b19b41f0735f) | The single-CTA register path keeps BF16 packed (four scores per `uint2`) and bins it with two packed conversions; FP32 bins as before | BF16 rows up to 16K: -8% to -19%; `persistent_topk` BF16 rows up to 32K: -24% to -31%; FP32 unchanged |

Measured and not adopted:

- Storing bins instead of recomputing them in the scatter pass: the spare shared memory now holds the extra BF16
  stages, overwriting the staged scores would break the overflow recovery that rereads them, and after the packed
  conversion a bin costs one conversion per two scores.
- A 32K single-CTA limit for BF16 (the registers FP32 uses for 16K): -21% to -25% just past 16K, but up to +40%
  at 32K with k=2048 and +3% at 16K, so it stays at 16K.
- Re-tuning the cluster sizes: forcing each of 2, 4, 8 and 16 on every shape above, the row-count rule is within
  2% of the best in 112 of 120 shapes. The others (16 rows at 512K and 1M, 1 row at 64K) depend on the row
  length, which the launcher does not know: lengths are on the device, and a CUDA graph captures
  `max_model_len`.
- In ncu, FP16 conversions were 2% to 4% of the original BF16 kernel's instructions, while the per-element loop
  (`LOP3`, `ISETP`, `BRA`) was about 45%; the pair loads cut the latter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report reasoning tokens in batched chat completions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` never sets `usage.completion_tokens_details`, so a server started with `--reasoning-parser` omits `reasoning_tokens` from batched responses while `/v1/chat/completions` reports them for the same conversation. This counts and sums them per conversation, the way the single-conversation path does. Follows #64757, which added the prompt-side `prompt_tokens_details` to the same endpoint.

## Claims

- With `--reasoning-parser`, `/v1/chat/completions/batch` returns `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` summed across conversations, including when `include_reasoning=false` (hidden reasoning is still generated and billed), matching `/v1/chat/completions`.
- Without a reasoning parser, `completion_tokens_details` stays `null`, as on `/v1/chat/completions`.

## Validation

New test `test_batch_reasoning_tokens_in_usage` in `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py`, through `RemoteOpenAIServer` with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3` (the module's existing server). It posts two conversations with `include_reasoning=false` and checks `0 < reasoning_tokens <= completion_tokens`.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py -k test_batch_reasoning_tokens_in_usage
```

Before the fix (main at cfa9f96):

```
>       assert details is not None
E       assert None is not None
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py:118: AssertionError
1 failed, 6 deselected
```

After the fix: `1 passed, 6 deselected`.

Usage for the same conversation on the same server (`max_tokens=64`, `temperature=0`, `include_reasoning=false`), after the fix; before it the batch `completion_tokens_details` is `null`:

| Endpoint | completion_tokens | reasoning_tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 64 | 63 |
| `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, the conversation twice | 128 | 126 |

Other checks after the fix:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_include_reasoning.py` (whole file) | 7 passed |
| `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, the new test only | 1 skipped, no server started |
| Unit tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py` (`-k` the six non-server tests) | 6 passed |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed (shellcheck skipped: no shell files, and its binary download timed out locally) |

Environment: CPU only (Intel i5-11300H, AVX-512), Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2, Python 3.12, `--enforce-eager`. The Python sources are this branch; the compiled CPU extensions come from the nightly CPU wheel for 2b009fc (20 commits behind, differing only in CUDA kernels). Validated on cfa9f96, then rebased onto 564ac0d; the commits in between only change `recipes/models/*.yaml`.

Not run locally: the server tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py` (they need `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, which serves without a reasoning parser, so this path only adds a `null` field there), and GPU CI. No model evaluation: model outputs are unchanged; only response usage changes.

## Details

- Root cause: `chat_completion_full_generator_batch` builds `UsageInfo` without `completion_tokens_details`, and never counts reasoning tokens even though each conversation already runs through its parser.
- The fix mirrors `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_full_generator`: call `parser.count_reasoning_tokens(output.token_ids)` after `parse`, and gate the details on `_include_reasoning_tokens_details`. It reuses `_make_completion_tokens_details`.
- Three existing unit tests build `OpenAIServingChatBatch` with `__new__`, so they now set `_include_reasoning_tokens_details = False` (as #64757 did for `enable_prompt_tokens_details`), and the fake parser gains `count_reasoning_tokens`.
- The Rust frontend serves `/v1/chat/completions/batch` as `not_supported`, so the new test is skipped when `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` is set, as the Rust frontend CI steps do (same pattern as `test_thinking_token_budget.py`). The Python-frontend steps run it.
- Docs: one sentence next to the `prompt_tokens_details` note for this endpoint in `openai_compatible_server.md`.

Not a duplicate: open and closed PRs and issues searched for "batch reasoning tokens", "completions/batch usage", "batched chat completions usage", "reasoning_tokens", `OpenAIServingChatBatch` and `batch_serving`. Related but different: #64757 (merged, prompt-side details only), #64041 (reasoning tokens on the derender endpoints), #58010 (hiding reasoning metadata in batch responses).

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used to find the bug, write the change and tests, and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Accept empty message content like the Python frontend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects empty user message content on `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/tokenize` with `400 BadRequestError: message content cannot be empty`, while the Python frontend renders it as a normal (empty) turn. This PR drops the Rust-only content check so both frontends accept the same requests.

Fixes #64433 (second bug, see #62741 below for the first one).

## Claims

- `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` accepts `{"role": "user", "content": ""}` and `{"role": "user", "content": []}` and returns `200` with non-empty `token_ids`.
- `POST /tokenize` accepts the same two payloads and returns `200` with non-empty `tokens`.
- `messages: []` is still rejected with `400` (`messages cannot be empty`); only the content check is removed.
- Rust/Python parity for chat-message validation is restored: the removed check was Rust-only and never existed in the Python frontend.

## Validation

Reproducer (unit/route level, no server or GPU needed):

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib empty_message_content
```

```
running 2 tests
test routes::tests::render_chat_accepts_empty_message_content ... ok
test routes::tests::tokenize_chat_accepts_empty_message_content ... ok

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 538 filtered out; finished in 0.03s
```


Other checks:

- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- Both routes reach the shared `validate_messages()` helper, so the change is exercised through the public HTTP entry points (`/v1/chat/completions/render`, `/tokenize`), not a test-only path.
- CI: `.buildkite/test_areas/rust_frontend_cargo.yaml` runs the whole `rust/` workspace test suite on any `rust/` change, so the new tests run in CI.

## Details

**Root cause.** `validate_messages()` in `rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/utils/types.rs` is shared by the chat-completions render path and the `/tokenize` chat form. It was introduced in #44222 together with `/tokenize` and added a `user`-message content check (`Text("")` / `Parts([])` → 400) that has no counterpart in the Python frontend (`vllm/renderers/`), which accepts empty content and renders an empty turn. Empty content is legal in the OpenAI schema, so the Rust frontend was stricter than both Python and the API spec.

**Design.** Minimal fix: delete the content loop, keep the `messages` non-empty check (both frontends still require at least one message). Net −8 lines in production code (low complexity, no new abstractions, no behaviour change outside these two routes); the only two call sites are `routes/openai/chat_completions/types.rs` and `routes/openai/tokenize/types.rs`.

**Tests.** `tokenize_chat_empty_message_content_returns_400` asserted the old (incorrect) behaviour and is replaced by `tokenize_chat_accepts_empty_message_content`; a new `render_chat_accepts_empty_message_content` covers the render route. Both assert `200` plus a non-empty token list for `""` and `[]`, so a regression that silently produces an empty prompt is also caught.

**Tradeoffs / limitations.** Empty turns are now tokenized (a few template control tokens) instead of rejected — same cost profile as Python. Validation was done at the route level; no local GPU/Python environment was available to run a side-by-side end-to-end comparison against the Python frontend, so the parity claim is based on the Python renderer's code path (no empty-content rejection there) rather than a live diff of responses.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep SW draft block a divisor of the primary block
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Related to #60174. **The correctness fix for #60174 is #55601**, not this PR. That bug is the mamba state column being seeded with the lowered `cache_config.block_size`. I briefly added the same one-line fix here (a24c836) without noticing #55601, and have reverted it (thanks @twu3202).

What this PR does: since #53007, a sliding-window layer whose largest fitting kernel block does not divide the primary block gets a padded page instead of an integer-scaled one. With a GDN hybrid target (1648-token block) and a SW DFlash2 drafter on a backend limited to `[16, 32, 64]` (FlashInfer on sm_120), the SW group runs on 64-token blocks. This:

- raises the scheduler block (LCM of all group blocks) from 1648 to 6592, the kind of LCM inflation #53007 set out to avoid;
- lowers `cache_config.block_size` to 64, which is what exposes the seeding bug in #55601;
- disables fine-grained prefix-cache hits (`Disabling fine-grained prefix-cache hits ... SlidingWindowManager`).

This PR keeps the SW block a divisor of the primary block, so `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` scales it as on v0.29.0. Configs where the chosen block already divides the primary block (the #53007 target case) are unchanged.

> **History.** Earlier versions of this PR described the padded SW page as the cause of #60174, then added the seeding fix. Both are superseded: the cause is the seeding bug, and its fix lives in #55601. Thanks to @sinmkd, @nej1gotnochill and @twu3202 for the reviews that got there.

## Validation

Single RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120), TP=1, vLLM 0.31.0 wheel with patches applied; Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (k=7), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, prefix caching on; fresh engine per run. 5-request replay with growing prefix (33K → 69K tokens):

| build | SW block / LCM | requests 3–5 | prefix-cache hit rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.31.0 | 64 / 6592 | degenerate (all-NaN logits) | – |
| + seeding fix (#55601 equivalent) | 64 / 6592 | coherent | 43.8% |
| + seeding fix + this PR | 1648 / 1648 | coherent | 71.2% |

Independent measurements:
- @stecasta, same-node A/B on DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + DFlash2 (k=8), only this change: KV groups go from 1648x14 + 64 (scheduler block 6592, fine-grained hits disabled) to all 1648; a 168-turn agentic replay goes from 26.1 to 20.0 min, prefix-cache hits 56.3% → 77.4%, decode tok/s unchanged.
- @twu3202 on sm_89 (SW-only arm: `kv lcm block sizes 1616`, 3 prefix hits vs 1 without it).

On its own, this PR also stops the #60174 corruption in my setup, but only because `min(group block sizes)` becomes the mamba block again. That masks the seeding bug and does not fix it.

Tests:
- `test_largest_kernel_block_within_divisor_of`: the new `divisor_of` option, including the fallback when no supported block divides the primary block.
- `test_sliding_window_spec_unifies_without_padding`: runs `Attention.get_kv_cache_spec` for a SW layer on a `[16, 32, 64]` backend, then `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size`. It asserts the SW page is scaled, not padded. With the fix disabled, the 1648 case fails and the 1536 case (unchanged path) passes.

These were run as plain assertions on the patched 0.31.0 install (no pytest there). CI covers `tests/v1/attention`. Lint: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` on the changed files.

## Details

`_largest_kernel_block_within` gets a `divisor_of` option. With it, the helper returns the largest fitting block that divides `divisor_of`, and falls back to the previous choice if none does. The SW branch passes the primary block when there is no `shared_page`. Without `divisor_of` the helper behaves exactly as before, so the existing `test_largest_kernel_block_within` cases are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate:** #55601 changes `mamba_hybrid.py`; this PR changes the SW kernel-block selection in `Attention.get_kv_cache_spec`. None of #55818, #59683, #58207, #54163 or #56552 touches that selection. I'm fine with this being reviewed after #55601, or closed if reviewers consider the padded layout acceptable.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Accept assistant turns without content like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend returns a 400 for an assistant message with no content (`content: null`, `content` omitted, or `content: []`) and no tool calls. The Python frontend accepts all three and renders an empty assistant turn, same as `content: ""`, which Rust already accepts. This brings Rust in line.

I ran into it while diffing render output between the two frontends. `{"role": "assistant", "content": null}` shows up a lot in replayed history (tool calls stripped by the client, placeholder turns), so it's worth matching.

## Claims

- Assistant turns with null, missing or `[]` content and no tool calls are accepted on `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/tokenize`, and render the same as `content: ""`.
- Token IDs match the Python frontend for these, including when the empty turn is the last message, with and without `continue_final_message`.

## Validation

`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `/v1/chat/completions/render`, messages `[user "hi", <assistant>, user "hi"]`:

| `<assistant>` | Python | Rust main | Rust this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{"role":"assistant","content":""}` | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| `{"role":"assistant","content":null}` | 200 | 400 | 200 |
| `{"role":"assistant"}` | 200 | 400 | 200 |
| `{"role":"assistant","content":[]}` | 200 | 400 | 200 |
| `{"role":"assistant","content":null,"tool_calls":[]}` | 200 | 400 | 200 |

The 400s are `Assistant messages must contain text, reasoning content, or tool_calls.` All the 200s return the same 20 token IDs. I also checked the empty turn as the final message: 18 tokens with default flags and 13 with `continue_final_message: true, add_generation_prompt: false`, same as Python in both cases.

The new route test sends all five variants (plus `content: null` with `reasoning: ""`) and checks for a 200 and identical token IDs. It fails on main at the `content: null` case and passes with the change.

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib -- render_chat_accepts_assistant_turn_without_content
cargo test -p vllm-server   # 546 passed
```

`cargo fmt`, clippy and pre-commit are clean on the changed files.

After the follow-up commit that removes the check instead of adding an empty text block: `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat --lib` passes (1060 tests), the route test fails with the check restored, and clippy is clean.

<details>
<summary>Screenshots (Rust main, this PR, Python)</summary>

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/rust-asst-empty-before.png)

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/rust-asst-empty-after.png)

![python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/rust-asst-empty-python.png)

</details>

## Details

`convert_message` in `chat_completions/convert.rs` builds an assistant message out of reasoning, text and tool-call blocks, and it bailed when that list came out empty. `content: ""` produces one empty text block, so it passed. The other forms of the same empty turn produced nothing and got rejected. The check is removed, so an assistant message may now have no blocks. Every renderer already treats that like one empty text block: they either join the text blocks or skip empty ones. So these turns render the same as `content: ""`. Leaving out a synthetic empty text block also keeps `content: null` without a text part, which is what Python passes to `openai`-format templates (`[]`). Rust's own non-streaming response returns `content: null` with no tool calls when the generated text is empty, so a client replaying that history used to get this 400.

Since #62424, an empty `reasoning: ""` is kept as its own block, and the check also rejected a turn whose only blocks were empty reasoning. With the check gone, `{"role": "assistant", "content": null, "reasoning": ""}` also renders as an empty turn instead of a 400, like Python; the route test covers it as a sixth variant.

I didn't find an existing issue or PR for this. #54368 is the Python side (null content with tool calls), and #63132 and #63137 are about the reasoning field aliases, so they don't overlap.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Stop advertising head_dim 64 in the b12x backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--attention-backend b12x` accepts head_dim 64 models at selection and then crashes after model load, at the first forward, inside the b12x paged planner (`no valid NUM_MMA_KV typed shared-memory allocation fits the device`). The b12x package cannot plan head_dim 64 decode at all, so this stops advertising 64 and lets selection fail fast. Fixes #63011.

## Claims

- head_dim 64 models with `--attention-backend b12x` are now rejected at backend selection with `Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.B12X is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['head_size not supported']`, before weights load, instead of crashing in CUDA graph capture.
- head_dim 128/192/256 are unchanged.
- One list entry removed, one unit test added. No kernel or runner changes.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, aarch64), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu132, flashinfer-python 0.7.2 (provides the `b12x` module), vLLM main @ 35d01660f.

```python
from vllm import LLM
LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", attention_config={"backend": "B12X"}, block_size=128, dtype="bfloat16")
```

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| startup | model loads, torch.compile runs, then `Capturing CUDA graphs` dies: `traits.py ... select_paged_forward_traits ... ValueError: no valid NUM_MMA_KV typed shared-memory allocation fits the device` | `ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.B12X is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['head_size not supported']` at selection |

Same before/after with `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct` (hybrid, head_dim 64). head_dim 128 (Qwen3-0.6B) still selects and runs b12x.

```
$ pytest tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py
44 passed in 38.41s   # DGX Spark, GB10; includes the 4 new parametrized cases
```

The new test fails on main (`supports_head_size(64)` is True there) and passes with this change. `pre-commit run --files ...` is clean.

## Details

Root cause is inside the b12x package (same in `flashinfer/experimental/b12x` on FlashInfer main and in the `b12x==1.5.1` wheel pinned by the `[b12x]` extra), reported upstream as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6977:

- `_paged_determine_cta_tile_q()` returns `cta_tile_q = 16` for every decode/verify plan, and for that family `select_paged_forward_traits()` only sweeps `num_mma_kv = 1`.
- `_paged_is_invalid()` keeps FA2's rule that `num_mma_d_vo == 4` (head_dim 64) with an odd `num_mma_kv` is invalid, so the single candidate is rejected and the sweep raises.
- The decode kernel itself (`PagedForwardKernel`, `base_use_paged_kv_tma_decode`) only accepts `num_mma_kv == 1` for the generic bf16 16-row family, so the two constraints contradict each other for head_dim 64. FlashInfer's own b12x paged tests only cover head_dim 128/192/256.

I tried the obvious package-side patches on the Spark before settling on this: forcing two KV tiles for head_dim 64 decode is rejected by the kernel constructor (`PagedForwardKernel now only supports exact-plane paged K/V TMA decode`), and relaxing the odd-tile rule for the decode family lets graph capture succeed but the head_dim 64 extend kernel warmup then compiles for 30 minutes without finishing (killed at the bound, twice). So head_dim 64 is not a working path in any released b12x, and the honest thing for vLLM to do is to not offer it. The package API has no head-dim capability query, so a static list is the only fail-fast available; 64 can be re-added, version-gated, once a b12x release supports it.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and this PR; I reviewed and tested the change on my own hardware.

---

## Overview

This is now independent, directly based on main `34d5de18cd8b`. [Review only this feature](https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/34d5de18cd8baf9f5958e45720858939863a7264...d6dd5d7f978059899d2f266e28a038f9fada6122); head `d6dd5d7f9780`. Rebuilt in response to Zifeng’s request to decouple the stacked PRs.

## Claims

- Reuse processed weights/scales across engine restarts with the validated CUTLASS backend.
- Preserve exact outputs, shared storage and required Python metadata; unsupported configurations remain rejected.
- Include only this feature and its necessary common plumbing beyond merged main.

## Validation

B300, November 4, exact source hashes verified against this head:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Layer/configuration regressions | 116 passed, 3 pre-existing skips in 251.81s |
| Real model: ordinary → fallback → IPC → second IPC | 1 passed in 113.40s |
| All changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed, including mypy, ruff and CI test tethering |

Both IPC loads forbid fallback. Exact greedy outputs use `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; layer tests also verify shared pointers and unchanged tensors. ```bash

The isolated runtime used Python 3.12, Torch 2.14/cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, process-local CUDAcompat13.4, and reused stable extensions from `5d55ef159`. Relevant CUTLASS FP8 C++ is unchanged; unrelated HiSparse binding and removed Qutlass-wrapper changes are outside these tests. This is targeted smoke/output equivalence, not a pristine full-source rebuild, full accuracy evaluation, performance benchmark, or upstream GPU CI result. No new skips, retries or weakened assertions were added. GPU occupancy guards prevented launches onto busy GPUs; other workloads were untouched.

<details>

</details>

The tensor/channel implementation from #63754 is already on main; its maintainer-removed redundant tests are not reintroduced.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --log-error-stack
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support `--log-error-stack` in the Rust frontend, so `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve ... --log-error-stack` starts instead of failing on an unsupported argument. Part of the logging argument parity item in #44280.

## Claims

- `--log-error-stack` is accepted and logs one ERROR event per error response built from `ApiError`.
- Like Python, it defaults to `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, on both the `vllm-rs serve` path and the Python-supervised `--args-json` path.

## Validation

- New CLI test `log_error_stack_defaults_to_server_dev_mode`: flag, env default, and explicit `false` overriding dev mode, for both the clap and `--args-json` paths.
- New route tests `log_error_stack_logs_error_responses` and `log_error_stack_disabled_logs_nothing` against the mock engine. With the layer disabled, the first one fails.
- `cargo test -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` pass.

Live check against `vllm-mock-engine`, following `rust/src/mock-engine/README.md`:

```bash
vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size-local 0 \
  --handshake-port 29550 --port 8765 --log-error-stack
vllm-mock-engine --handshake-address tcp://127.0.0.1:29550
```

One valid chat request (200), then a wrong model, broken JSON, and `max_tokens: -5`. Each failure logs one ERROR event and the valid request logs none:

```
INFO  [access_log.rs:47] HTTP response ... status=200 ...
ERROR [error_log.rs:22] Error response method=POST path="/v1/chat/completions" status=404 error_type="NotFoundError" error="The model `nope` does not exist."
ERROR [error_log.rs:22] Error response method=POST path="/v1/chat/completions" status=400 error_type="Bad Request" error="Failed to parse the request body as JSON: key must be a string at line 1 column 2"
ERROR [error_log.rs:22] Error response method=POST path="/v1/chat/completions" status=400 error_type="Bad Request" error="Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: max_tokens: invalid value: integer `-5`, expected u32 at line 1 column 86"
```

Error replies to clients are unchanged.

## Details

`ApiError::into_response` attaches its `ErrorResponse` to the response extensions, and a `log_error_response` middleware, installed only when the flag is set, logs it.

Python only forwards non-default args in `--args-json`, and the default of `log_error_stack` is `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`. So the Rust side reads `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE` itself, through a hidden env-bound arg and `apply_env_fallbacks`, the same way `VLLM_SKIP_MODEL_NAME_VALIDATION` works.

Deviations from Python:

- Rust errors have no stack trace, so the event logs the error message instead. For internal errors the message already includes the source chain.
- Python logs its internal request ID. That ID is not available where `ApiError` becomes a response, so the event logs method and path instead.
- Only `ApiError` responses are logged. Python also logs `HTTPException`s such as unrouted 404s. Rust's unrouted 404s and auth 401s do not go through `ApiError`, so they are not logged.
- `--no-log-error-stack` is not accepted on the `vllm-rs` CLI; use `--log-error-stack false`. This matches earlier boolean flag ports. Python passes the value through `--args-json`, so `vllm serve --no-log-error-stack` still works.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Return lazily offloaded GPU blocks to the eviction end
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In lazy mode, SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler offloads the cached blocks at the eviction end of the GPU free queue, then releases them with free_blocks, which appends cached blocks as most recently used. The blocks the CPU now holds outlive fresher blocks it doesn't hold, so the allocator evicts those instead. The scan keeps offloading new blocks, and the CPU cache turns over faster than it can serve hits.

* Adds evict_first to BlockPool.free_blocks (off by default) to free cached blocks to the front of the queue.
* Lazy store completion uses it, eager mode and abandoned stores are unchanged.
* Adds test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end, which fails without the fix.

## Test Plan

Regression test fails on `main`

```bash
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k test_lazy_store_returns_blocks_to_eviction_end
```

The bug only affects throughput when the lazy CPU tier is smaller than the GPU KV cache, and the GPU free queue is
much longer than one lazy scan (for example `2 × max_num_batched_tokens` tokens). 

With a small GPU cache, each scan covers the whole free queue, so block order doesn't matter: in a run with a 1,024-block GPU cache on one L4, `main` and this branch served the same CPU hits.

## Test Result

## AI assistance

Claude helped with debugging this problem and wrote the fix, the code changes were reviewed by a human

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Reject stacked weights that received only some shards
commits.pr_body: ## Overview `track_weights_loading` only diffs parameter names, so `qkv_proj.weight` counts as loaded once any one shard is written. A checkpoint missing every `v_proj` loads cleanly and serves uninitialized rows. Follow-up to #55911 agreed with @hmellor. ## Claims - A stacked parameter (`MergedColumnParallelLinear`, `QKVParallelLinear` and their subclasses) that received only some shards now fails at load, naming the parameter and the missing shard ids. - Same gate as the existing check (unquantized by default, `enable_weights_track` to force). Valid checkpoints are untouched. ## Validation `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_stacked_shard_tracking.py` → 7 passed. Qwen3-0.6B on H100, tensors deleted from the safetensors file, loaded via `LLM`: | Checkpoint | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | untouched | OK | OK | | all `v_proj` removed | loads, generates `!!!!!!!!` | `ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight.v', …}` | | `layers.3.mlp.up_proj` removed | loads, wrong text | `ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.3.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight.1'}` | No eval needed: weights of a valid checkpoint are bitwise unchanged. ## Details New base `StackedColumnParallelLinear`: each `weight_loader`/`weight_loader_v2` records the shard it wrote on the param, and `pop_missing_shards()` reports expected shards that never arrived, then clears the record so a later load is graded on its own. Shards with zero rows on the rank are never expected. The loader runs it after the existing name check. `shard_ids` is now the single declaration per class. --- Need help on this PR? commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Initialize Mistral EAGLE weight-loader state
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix draft weight loading for Mistral EAGLE models, including [Mistral Small 4 EAGLE](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle).

## Claims

- Initialize the shared-expert state used by the inherited weight loader.
- Initialize `hidden_size`, which the inherited forward path reads during sequence-parallel gathering.

## Validation

CPU: five tests passed on `b14e2f279` plus this patch. Pre-commit passed, including mypy. The new regression constructs a real draft model and checks the loaded weight tensor.

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft weight loading | `AttributeError: 'EagleMistralLarge3Model' object has no attribute 'fused_shared_expert_layers'` | Loads the norm weight with exact tensor equality |

GPU: B200 x1 / TP1, Mistral Small 4 NVFP4 with its public EAGLE draft, vLLM `b14e2f279` plus this patch, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130. Context 8192, GMU 0.85, max sequences 8, prefix caching off. Both patched runs used Model Runner V2.

| Configuration | Startup and generation | GSM8K smoke | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unpatched EAGLE, k=3 | Startup fails with the missing attribute above | — | — |
| Target only | Generates | 28/32 | — |
| Patched EAGLE, k=3, eager | Generates; nonzero draft acceptance | 28/32 | 3.25 |
| Patched EAGLE, k=3, non-eager | Generates; nonzero draft acceptance | 30/32 | 3.18 |

Acceptance length includes one target-generated token; its maximum is `k + 1`. The corresponding draft acceptance rates were 75.0% and 72.8%.

The smoke uses the first 32 GSM8K test questions, five-shot prompts, greedy decoding and a 512-token cap. No GSM8K response reached the cap. Generation was also checked on eight math/coding prompts at batches 1 and 8 with a 128-token cap. Greedy outputs differ between target-only and speculative decoding.

Public checkpoints: [NVFP4 target](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4/tree/45331841b631f4e281df8e959ea3cc9beb84298a), [EAGLE draft](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle/tree/9a8ea22dca0161ff7af7879f4a0000f65314797d).

<details>
<summary>CPU test commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_mistral_large_3_eagle.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_mistral_large_3_eagle.py
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>GPU reproducer</summary>

From a vLLM checkout with GPU dependencies installed:

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k_offline

llm = LLM(
    model="mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4",
    revision="45331841b631f4e281df8e959ea3cc9beb84298a",
    config_format="mistral", load_format="mistral", tokenizer_mode="mistral",
    tensor_parallel_size=1, max_model_len=8192,
    max_num_seqs=8, max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, enable_prefix_caching=False,
    disable_log_stats=False, generation_config="vllm", seed=42,
    enforce_eager=True,
    attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_MLA"},
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0},
    speculative_config={
        "model": "mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-eagle",
        "revision": "9a8ea22dca0161ff7af7879f4a0000f65314797d",
        "method": "eagle", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
        "max_model_len": 8192,
    },
)
print(llm.chat(
    [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 multiplied by 23? Show the calculation."}],
    SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, seed=42),
))
print(evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=32, num_shots=5, max_tokens=512))
print([metric for metric in llm.get_metrics() if "spec_decode" in metric.name])
```

Repeat with `enforce_eager=False` for non-eager execution. Omit `speculative_config` for the target-only reference. The checked-in loader regression runs in Model Executor CI; the real-weight 119B checks were run separately on B200.

</details>

## Details

`EagleMistralLarge3Model` inherits `load_weights` and `forward` from `DeepseekV2Model` but skips its constructor. The draft constructor does not initialize the shared-expert state that the weight loader reads, so loading fails even for a dense draft.

Use the same helper as the parent to derive fused shared-expert layers from the constructed model. This also preserves the parent's policy checks if a draft contains MoE layers.

Based on Ruben Debien's open [#61369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61369), adapted to the per-layer shared-expert API introduced by [#61457](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61457). The earlier patch initializes the old boolean flag using a helper that no longer exists on main.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Share the QSA top-k buffer across layers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) allocated one QSA top-k selection buffer per QSA layer (`max_num_batched_tokens x (indexer_budget + compress_ratio)` int32 each). This PR allocates one buffer on `Qwen4ExpModel` and passes it to every QSA layer, as DeepSeek V3.2/V4, GLM-5.3-Flash and MiniMax-M3 already do. The MTP drafter now reuses the target buffer through the existing proposer sharing (`load_eagle_model` / `llm_base_proposer`).

## Claims

- Removes 12 of the 13 per-layer buffers on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (12 QSA layers + 1 MTP layer). With the default `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` each buffer is 128 MiB, so about 1.5 GiB/GPU moves to the KV cache (measured +1.52 GiB). The saving scales with `max_num_batched_tokens`, so large-chunk prefill deployments gain more.
- No accuracy or MTP acceptance change.

## Validation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on 1x GB200 node, `-tp 4 -ep --enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, default `max_num_batched_tokens` (16384). Baseline is `main` at 5225a1f17f; same node type, same command.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV cache memory (per GPU) | 143.60 GiB | 145.12 GiB (+1.52 GiB) |
| GPU KV cache size | 9,044,352 tokens | 9,151,208 tokens (+1.2%) |
| gsm8k (20-shot, chat, 1319 q) | 0.966 | 0.964 |
| MTP draft acceptance (whole gsm8k run) | 82.68% | 82.69% |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 -tp 4 -ep --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 20 --num-questions 1319 \
  --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --max-tokens 1024 --max-concurrency 64
```

Unit tests (GB200): `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_tpsp.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py` -> 15 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only).

## Details

- Sharing is safe because each QSA layer writes its selection and the sparse attention reads it within the same layer call, and Qwen4Exp QSA already rejects DBO/microbatching, so layers never interleave.
- MTP: the drafter allocates its own buffer at construction (like the other sparse MTP models) and the proposer replaces it with the target's. The target does not run between draft steps, and the drafter runs one layer per step, so `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` (step-0 rows reused by later steps) keeps working.
- Only the NVIDIA implementation is changed. The ROCm implementation (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/`) has the same per-layer buffer; I'll follow up there once I can validate on ROCm.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR shares this buffer. #59279/#61242/#61728 (QSA DCP) only touch the comment next to it.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Quantization] Support AWQ/GPTQ Marlin cache restarts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Allow the weight-cache daemon to reuse AWQ/GPTQ linear weights already packed for Marlin across engine restarts. Related to #56049; updated against main `8cf1277362aef963a71cf6860c28387acf6ecb90`.

## Claims

- Support AWQ INT4 and symmetric GPTQ INT4/INT8 linear weights with the actual Marlin kernel and FP16/BF16 activations.
- Preserve shared repacked weights, scales, zero points and padded bias without repeating checkpoint conversion or Marlin transformations.
- Continue rejecting other kernels, INT8/FP8 activation overrides and AWQ/GPTQ MoE.

## Validation

November 3 integration update: preserve the GPTQ batch-invariant ordinary-loading path from #60479 and restore the symmetric Marlin runtime zero-point name after #62407. The latter now keeps checkpoint `qzeros` registered and reads a separate empty `w_zp`; an IPC attachment must restore that kernel metadata and mark checkpoint `qzeros` retired. No tensor data is transformed on attachment. The existing tests reproduced 5 failures (GPTQ real-model IPC and four layer cases) before this correction, with 6 passing. Final results: **11 passed, 68 deselected in 244.14s** on B300 (same two pinned real models, ordinary/fallback/IPC/restart with `fallback=False`, plus nine layer/boundary cases). A real CPU/Gloo GPTQ construction check also preserves checkpoint tensors in batch-invariant mode and rejects Marlin IPC without initializing CUDA. Changed-file hooks pass, including mypy and CI tethering. Existing torch/fork deprecation warnings remain; no L4 Buildkite run is claimed.


B300, TP1. The two real-model cases use FP16, eager execution, TRITON_ATTN, explicitly selected Marlin, two prompts × 16 generated tokens, and prompt/sample top-5 logprobs. Each compares ordinary loading → missing-daemon disk fallback → IPC → second IPC; both IPC starts set `fallback=False`. Comparison uses the existing `check_logprobs_close` helper. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` is intentional: AWQ and GPTQ use unpacked implementations when enabled, and Marlin does not guarantee batch invariance.

| Check | Before implementation | After implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B AWQ and GPTQ-INT4 checkpoints | 2 failed, 118.22s; ordinary/fallback generation works, both daemons reject their quant method | 2 passed, 144.56s, all four loading paths |
| Real fused INT4 layers, aligned/padded outputs and bias | 4 failed, 32.41s: pre-processed weights rejected | All pass, with exact output/shape/shared-pointer/tensor-content checks across two attachments |
| Final layer/boundary suite, including GPTQ INT8/channelwise BF16 and actual Triton/A8 rejection | — | 9 passed, 12.92s |
| Existing AWQ/GPTQ config and weight-cache regressions | — | 76 passed, 18 deselected, 63.38s |
| Changed-file hooks | — | Passed, including mypy, ruff and CI test tethering |

Checkpoints: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-AWQ` at `db09cd27ead7fee40cdee309693cf83601b9c899`; `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4` at `c34a4a91629f09f73a285f32dbd26106b033c654`. INT8/BF16 and padded outputs are covered by real CUDA layers, not a complete INT8 checkpoint. This is cache-versus-ordinary output equivalence, not quantization accuracy against BF16 or a performance benchmark. Multi-GPU, other hardware and other kernels are not claimed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and baseline evidence</summary>

```bash
# Run each on an idle GPU; HF_HUB_OFFLINE assumes the pinned models are cached.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k marlin_preprocessed -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k ipc_cache_marlin -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_auto_awq.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'not quantization_method and not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not marlin' -q
```

Apply the new tests to main `6376fda7a9` without the two production changes to reproduce the failures. Before implementation, the real daemons report:

```text
UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: layer model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj:
AutoAWQMarlinLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights.
UnsupportedQuantForIPCError: layer model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj:
AutoGPTQLinearMethod does not support loading from pre-processed weights.
2 failed, 74 deselected, 16 warnings in 118.22s
```

Host-specific environment: its precompiled Marlin path first failed with unsupported PTX during ordinary loading. Baseline and passing results above both use process-local `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/cuda-compat-13-4/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat`, containing NVIDIA's checksum-verified `cuda-compat-13-4` package `615.71.10-1ubuntu1`, as supported by [NVIDIA's compatibility matrix](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/latest/forward-compatibility.html). It was extracted under the user's task directory; the host driver and shared Python environment were not modified. Initial environment failures and corrected negative-test setup errors are retained separately and are not represented as cache bug reproductions. Runs emit existing torch/fork deprecation warnings.

</details>

## Details

Both methods previously rejected daemon caching even though ordinary Marlin loading worked. Their kernel configuration is constructed before post-load processing. Normal post-load work converts AWQ packing and/or repacks weights, permutes scales/zero points, pads/permutates bias and selects the symmetric GPTQ runtime zero-point name. IPC already supplies transformed tensors; the GPTQ attachment restores the runtime name and retirement metadata. Opt in only the actual `MarlinLinearKernel` with FP16/BF16 activations, and return before those transformations on the pre-processed path. No common loading interface, kernel implementation, scheduler/model-runner change or steady-state synchronization is added.

Reuse the existing daemon, generation and comparison helpers. The L4 Marlin Preload CI step selects the real-model and layer/boundary cases and tracks their source dependencies. Local validation is B300; L4 Buildkite execution is not claimed. The preload guide documents commands, defaults and exclusions, with links from the AWQ/GPTQ guides.

Duplicate checks covered current #56049/comments, issue-linked drafts and open Marlin-preload/AWQ/GPTQ-cache searches. #61908 introduces a different on-disk AWQ-v2 format, while #60479 changes GPTQ batch-invariant execution; neither restores daemon IPC weights. Existing FP8/FP4 cache drafts do not cover this path.

AI assistance: Codex implemented and ran the recorded validation at the submitter's request. This draft is for human review; no completed human approval or human-run tests are asserted.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix tensor conversion in audio parsing and hashing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix tensor-to-NumPy conversion in audio input parsing and shared multimodal hashing.

Following @DarkLight1337's suggestion, I checked the other explicit conversion paths and confirmed the same gradient-related failure in multimodal hashing.

## Claims

- Handle CUDA and gradient-tracking audio tensors by detaching and moving them to CPU before NumPy conversion.
- Detach tensors before hashing, covering image/video tensors and precomputed audio embeddings.
- Add regression coverage and document direct audio Tensor inputs.

## Validation

Before the fixes, the audio model test and the three CPU hashing cases failed with:

```text
RuntimeError: Can't call numpy() on Tensor that requires grad.
```

After the fixes:

| Environment | Validation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS, CPU | Full parser and hasher suites | 57 passed, 4 skipped |
| DGX Spark, CPU/CUDA | New hashing regression for image, video, and audio embeddings | 6 passed |
| DGX Spark | Full parser suite | 34 passed |
| DGX Spark | Whisper Tiny `LLM.generate()` regression | 1 passed |

The hashing tests verify exact hash equality with detached reference tensors.

The Whisper test uses real weights and the `mary_had_lamb` audio sample. It compares gradient-tracking CPU tensors, CUDA tensors, and gradient-tracking CUDA tensors with a NumPy reference using `check_logprobs_close`.

Image/video and embedding coverage exercises parsing and hashing; the real-model test covers raw audio.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

Local parser and hasher suites:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  ../vllm-dev/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_parse.py \

```

The new hashing regression was run before and after changing the hasher:

```sh

  ../vllm-dev/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \

  -q --tb=short
```

```sh
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR \

tests/multimodal/test_parse.py::test_hash_parsed_tensor_with_grad \
```

```sh
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR \
```

## Details

Audio parsing previously called `.numpy()` directly, which fails for CUDA tensors and tensors requiring gradients.

The shared multimodal hasher already moved tensors to CPU, but did not detach them before calling `.numpy()`. Adding `detach()` fixes gradient-tracking inputs while preserving the hashes produced for their detached equivalents.

The DGX validation used this branch's Python source with installed vLLM 0.31.0 native extensions. Startup reported missing Triton kernels and unavailable FlashInfer sampling, but Whisper inference completed. These tests validate input compatibility, not model accuracy.

commits.pr_title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Add per-GPU device names for MooncakeStoreConnector
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in `device_name_per_gpu` key to the Mooncake Store config: RDMA device names indexed by physical GPU ID, of which each rank's store client gets only its own GPU's entry. `device_name` keeps the all-HCAs behaviour from #43799. Companion to kvcache-ai/Mooncake#5151.

## Claims

- `setup_mooncake_store` passes the current GPU's entry when the key is set, else `device_name` as before. This covers MooncakeStoreConnector and the Mooncake EC connector's embedding store, both built in GPU workers.
- The two keys are mutually exclusive. An empty list, a blank entry or a GPU with no entry raises `ValueError`. Sleep mode accepts either key.
- An entry may list several devices, so a B300 host can give each GPU its two HCAs.

## Validation

- `whx/mooncake-store-per-gpu-nic @ b74843e87`: `test_mooncake_store_worker.py` 254 passed, including the new selection and invalid-config tests; 1 setup error because I ran without `tests/conftest.py` (the `caplog_vllm` fixture). pre-commit clean.
- Not from this branch: Kimi-K3 1P1D on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X with an equivalent runtime patch (each rank limited to `rdma<physical GPU>`). The prefill Store registered 209 GiB per rank and the benchmark passed. Without it, every rank tried all 8 NICs and Store init failed (details below).

## Details

Why not all NICs: when a rank's NICs span NUMA nodes, Mooncake maps the global segment with 4KB pages, and on MI355X `ibv_reg_mr` failed with EINVAL within each rank's first 2 GiB. kvcache-ai/Mooncake#5151 fixes the allocation; whether 8 ranks then fit on every NIC is untested, and one NIC per GPU is the setup measured here.

#42689 picked one CSV entry by GPU index, which #43799 removed for B300 (8 GPUs, 16 HCAs). An explicit list keeps that case expressible and changes no default. AI-assisted (Claude in Cursor).

<details><summary>Failing run without per-GPU NICs</summary>

```
real_client.cpp:1162] NUMA-segmented mode: NIC NUMA nodes=[0,1]
mmap_buffer.cpp:355] Allocated NUMA-segmented buffer: 224873414656 bytes, 2 regions, page_size=4096, nodes=[0,1]
rdma_context.cpp:803] Failed to register memory 0x74c143200000 length 67108864 dmabuf_offset 0 on rdma5 MC_RDMA_DATA_DIRECT=0: Invalid argument [22]
```

92 such failures, all on rdma5, across all 8 ranks. Store-process AnonHugePages per rank: 2,967,552 kB here, 222,558,208 kB with one NIC per GPU on the same node.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Handle buffered JSON embedding responses in run-batch
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix batch embedding responses after #58660. The shared serializer returns a plain `Response`, which `run-batch` currently misidentifies as a stream and writes as a 400 error.

## Claims

- Decode buffered JSON responses while continuing to reject streams.
- Make the existing embedding batch test check successful results and the expected unknown-model error, rather than just the output schema.

## Validation

Ran the real `vllm run-batch` CLI on an Apple M4 Pro CPU with `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, using the four requests from `INPUT_EMBEDDING_BATCH`:

| Result | Main (`60a7d568f`) | With fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three valid requests | 400: `Request must not be sent in stream mode` | 200, each with 384 finite embedding values |
| Unknown model | 404 | 404 |
| CLI exit code | 0 | 0 |

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind vllm run-batch \
  -i embeddings.jsonl -o results.jsonl \
  --model intfloat/multilingual-e5-small \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.1 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 4
```

The model-backed result above was recorded before this rebase using PyTorch 2.14.0 and model snapshot `614241f622f53c4eeff9890bdc4f31cfecc418b3`. The memory setting accommodates the RAM available on this machine. On the rebased head, the local CPU extension needs rebuilding: the CLI stops before serving because it lacks `prepare_prefill_inputs_cpu`. The focused response tests and pre-commit pass on the rebased head.

The focused response tests fail on main for the shared serializer and pass with this fix:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py \
  -k 'batch_embedding_json_responses or batch_rejects_json_stream' -q
```

`--noconftest` avoids a macOS crash in the global PyTorch cleanup fixture. Calling `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache()` without importing vLLM reproduces it. No fixture is changed in this PR. The model-backed validation above ran the actual CLI and engine separately.

Pre-commit passes, including mypy and test tethering. The existing `entrypoints-unit-tests` Buildkite job selects these tests.

## Details

Accept non-streaming `application/json` responses at the batch boundary and parse their bytes with the cached response adapter, leaving the shared serializer unchanged. Add a CLI documentation example explaining per-request status and errors.

No open PR was found for this regression. #63005 changes TypeAdapter caching in the same function but retains the `JSONResponse` check, so it addresses a separate issue. Closed #39248 concerned `ORJSONResponse`, which inherits `JSONResponse`; this failure involves a plain `Response`.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.
