## Overview

Follow-up to #64215. Canary transcription requests without `language` now return HTTP 400, and Canary translation gets CI coverage.

## Claims

- `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` cannot detect the audio's language, but transcription defaulted a missing `language` to `en` and only logged a server warning, so non-English audio came back as English text with HTTP 200. It now fails with HTTP 400, as translation already does since #64215.
- `test_translation_validation.py` now covers Canary: one en->de translation, plus the 400s for a missing `language` and a non-English pair (de->fr).

## Validation

German speech (macOS `say -v Anna`), `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`, CPU (M5 Pro):

| `language` | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omitted | 200 `"Good morning, today is the weather in Berlin sunny and warm, ..."` | 400 `Canary cannot detect the audio's language; pass language (...)` |
| `de` | 200 `"Guten Morgen, heute ist das Wetter in Berlin sonnig und warm, ..."` | 200, unchanged |

```
pytest -v -s "tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py::test_canary_translation"
main:    E   Failed: DID NOT RAISE BadRequestError   (transcription without language -> 200 OK)
this PR: 1 passed in 45.08s
```

The en->de output matches Transformers `generate` (fp32): "Mary hatte ein kleines Lamm ...". I did not use the module's `foscolo` it->en clip because canary-1b-v2 leaves most of that poem in Italian, in Transformers too. The WER test already sends `language="en"`, so its result does not change.

## Details

This departs from Cohere ASR, FunASR and FireRedASR2, which default to `en` with a warning. For Canary, that default produced an English translation labelled as a transcription. The test uses the platform default attention backend, like the Canary WER test, because the file's ROCm helper selects `ROCM_AITER_FA`, which rejects cross-attention. The docs note that Canary requires `language` and translates to or from English only.

No duplicate: there are no open PRs for Canary (searched `canary-1b-v2`, `CanaryForConditionalGeneration`).

commits.pr_title: [XPU] fix case test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py and test_mm_prefix_lm.py
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Fix two independent root causes behind three failed jobs in [Intel CI build 16461](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/16461):

Align the producer and consumer block sizes in the P2P lifecycle regression test.
Pad Triton prefill attention’s head-dimension tile to at least 16.

## Root Cause
P2P lifecycle test: incompatible default block sizes
The producer uses native LLM, while the consumer uses VllmRunner. With batch invariance enabled, both select Triton Attention, but their effective defaults differ on XPU:

`test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py` :
Producer: 16 tokens per block.
Consumer: 64 tokens per block.
Consequently, their offloaded blocks have different byte sizes (368640 versus 1474560). The P2P handshake correctly rejects this incompatible layout. The test then fails at assert buffered.is_set() because no transfer completion arrives—not because buffered completion handling is broken.

Set block_size=16 in the shared engine parameters so both peers use the same layout. Also assert that the disconnect was injected, ensuring the test exercises its intended failure ordering rather than passing without reaching it.

`test_mm_prefix_lm.py` :
Multimodal tests: insufficient Triton dot tile width
Both multimodal jobs fail in test_mm_prefix_lm_cache_hit_inside_image. Its tiny Gemma3 model has a vision attention head dimension of 8.

The prefill kernel previously used next_power_of_2(head_dim), producing a tile width of 8. For tl.dot(p, v, acc), this is the output dimension, but the XPU Triton compiler requires it to be at least 16:


Use max(16, next_power_of_2(head_dim)). Existing masks zero-fill padded loads and restrict output stores to the actual head dimension. Tile widths for head dimensions of 16 or greater remain unchanged.

## Claims

commits.pr_title: [CI] Enroll RL Entrypoints in automatic sharding
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enrolls RL Entrypoints and its AMD mirror in `automatic_shard`. The step exported `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` on its own line between its two pytest commands, and the planner only accepts plain pytest commands after the first one, so an enrollment flag alone would be ignored. This PR sets the variable on the second pytest command instead.

## Claims

| Job | Plan |
|---|---|
| `rl-entrypoints-tests` | 1 shard |
| its AMD mirror | 1 shard |

- **Same environment per command as before.** The first command (`weight_transfer`) still runs without the variable, and the second still runs with it. Nothing later in the step read the exported value.
- One-shard plans run the same tests as on main, as one job, and split by themselves once their tests grow.

## Validation

- ci-infra's `split_commands` rejects the current commands and accepts the new ones.
- The sharding harness and the generator's own enrollment gate both accept the step and its mirror, as one job.
- `split_check.py` finds no step whose jobs each run the whole suite.
- The step and its mirror pass on recent main builds, nightly included.
- `/ci run` on this head, compared per command against main's test counts.

## Details

- **Timing label.** Main's per-command timings key on the full command text, so the second command gets a new label. Until main records it, the step may run as one job, which is what the plan says anyway.
- **Timeouts unchanged.** `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Stop binding --data-parallel-rank to VLLM_DP_RANK
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stop binding `vllm-rs serve --data-parallel-rank` to the `VLLM_DP_RANK` environment variable. An exported `VLLM_DP_RANK` silently put the Rust frontend into external DP load balancing with that rank, while `vllm serve` turns on external LB only from the CLI flag.

## Claims

- `VLLM_DP_RANK` in the environment no longer changes how `vllm-rs serve` sets up data parallelism; with `--data-parallel-size 4` it now selects internal LB, as `vllm serve` does.
- `--data-parallel-rank` keeps working: an explicit rank still selects external LB.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2511 tests run: 2511 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `data_parallel_rank_is_not_bound_to_vllm_dp_rank` asserts the arg has no env binding (process env is shared across tests, and the crate has no env-isolated harness). It fails with the binding restored.
- Checked with separate processes: `VLLM_DP_RANK=1 --data-parallel-size 4` selects external LB on `main` and internal LB with this change; an explicit `--data-parallel-rank 3` selects external LB on both.

## Details

- **Status quo.** `DataParallelLbArgs::data_parallel_rank` (`rust/src/managed-engine/src/data_parallel.rs`) is declared with `env = "VLLM_DP_RANK"`. vllm-project/vllm#64451 kept that binding when it moved the arg from an unsupported marker, where the same export used to fail startup.
- **Python.** `vllm serve` turns on external LB from `args.data_parallel_rank` (`vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py`). `VLLM_DP_RANK` (`vllm/envs.py`) is read only in `ParallelConfig`'s environment fallback (`vllm/config/parallel.py`), used for example by offline SPMD, and nothing in vLLM sets it for child processes.
- **Change.** Drop the binding. `DataParallelLbArgs::resolve` reads only the parsed arg, and clap's declaration is where the environment entered it, so that is the layer to change.
- **Behavior change.** A deployment that relied on an exported `VLLM_DP_RANK` to select external LB under `vllm-rs serve` must pass `--data-parallel-rank`, as `vllm serve` requires.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the `VLLM_DP_RANK` binding of the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for `VLLM_DP_RANK` and Rust frontend data-parallel arguments; vllm-project/vllm#64426 touches multi-port DP serving, not this arg). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept Python underscore and dotted flag forms under vllm-rs serve
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make `vllm-rs serve` accept the two argv spellings Python's `FlexibleArgumentParser` rewrites: underscores in long flag names (`--served_model_name`) and dotted forms of JSON flags (`--hf-overrides.rope_scaling.factor 4`). Today both reach only the managed Python engine, and the Rust frontend silently keeps its default for flags it declares itself.

## Claims

- Long flag names are normalized like Python: `_` becomes `-` up to the first `.` or `=`, so `--served_model_name qwen` and `--max_model_len=1024` configure the Rust frontend. Keys after the first `.` keep their underscores.
- Dotted forms of every flag `vllm-rs serve` declares (for example `--hf-overrides.*`, `--structured-outputs-config.*`, `--default-chat-template-kwargs.*`) are merged into one `--<flag> <JSON>` with Python's rules, so the Rust tokenizer, model config, structured-output backend and chat template kwargs see the override. Shared flags still reach the engine, unknown keys included.
- Dotted forms of engine-only flags (for example `--compilation-config.mode 3`) go to Python unchanged, as before.
- The Python-supervised path (`vllm serve` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) is unaffected: it already hands Rust the merged values through `--args-json`.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2513 tests run: 2513 passed, 13 skipped
```

New tests in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/tests.rs`, through `Cli::try_parse_from` to the parsed args and the managed-engine argv:

- `serve_args_accept_python_underscore_flag_names`: without the first commit, `served_model_name` stays empty.
- `serve_args_merge_dotted_forms_of_frontend_flags`: nested keys, inline `=` values, `32k`/`4K`/`1.5K`, list append, shared-flag forwarding, and an engine-only dotted flag left for Python; fails without the second commit.
- `serve_args_reject_dotted_frontend_flag_without_value`.

The merge rules were checked against Python's parser, for example `--hf-overrides.b 2 --hf-overrides.n 32k --hf-overrides.m 1.5K` gives `{"b": 2, "n": 32000, "m": "1.5K"}` on both.

## Details

Python's `FlexibleArgumentParser` rewrites argv before argparse runs:

- underscores in a long flag name become dashes, up to the first `.` or `=`;
- every dotted form `--<flag>.<key>[.<key>...] <value>` is merged into one `--<flag> <JSON object>` per flag, appended after the other arguments.

Under `vllm-rs serve`, the argv repartitioner (`repartition_managed_engine_args`, `rust/src/managed-engine/src/cli.rs`) keeps a flag on the Rust side only when its head matches a clap name exactly; everything else goes to the managed Python engine. So an underscore spelling or a dotted form of a flag Rust declares reached only the engine. Examples: `--served_model_name`, `--structured-outputs-config.backend guidance` (Rust keeps compiling with xgrammar), `--default-chat-template-kwargs.enable_thinking false`, `--hf-overrides.*`.

One commit per part:

1. **Underscore spellings.** The repartitioner normalizes long flag names like Python, next to the existing `-tp`-style alias normalization. Forwarded flags are normalized too, which Python would do anyway.
2. **Dotted forms of Rust-declared flags.** Before routing, `merge_dotted_frontend_args` merges `--<flag>.<path>` for every flag `vllm-rs serve` declares, with Python's rules: the value is parsed as JSON, then as a human-readable integer (`32k`, `4K`, ported from `human_readable_int`), and otherwise kept as a string; `<key>+ a,b` appends list elements; objects merge key by key and lists concatenate (`recursive_dict_update`). The merged `--<flag> <JSON>` is appended and goes to clap. Shared flags (`--hf-overrides`, `--structured-outputs-config`, `--profiler-config`, `--limit-mm-per-prompt`) reach the engine through the existing re-serialization, which keeps unknown keys (`#[serde(flatten)]` extras; `HfOverrides` is a map).

**Layering.** The consumer is clap's parse of `vllm-rs serve` argv, and the repartitioner is the one place that turns Python-style argv into it (it already absorbs Python's multi-character aliases), so both rewrites live there. `vllm-rs frontend` and `vllm-rs render` parse with clap directly and keep rejecting these spellings with a clap error.

**Differences from Python.**

- A dotted form combined with the full JSON flag (`--hf-overrides '{...}' --hf-overrides.x 1`) is a clap error ("cannot be used multiple times"), like any repeated Rust flag; Python keeps the last occurrence, which silently drops the full JSON.
- A dotted flag with no value is a clap error; Python fails with an `IndexError` traceback.
- Python logs a warning for duplicate dotted keys; Rust overwrites silently with the same result.
- `int()` corner cases that are not JSON (`1_000`) stay strings.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes how `vllm-rs serve` handles underscore or dotted flag spellings (searched open Rust frontend PRs for argument parsing, dotted flags and `FlexibleArgumentParser`). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Coerce replayed tool-call arguments that are not an object
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In the Rust frontend, coerce replayed assistant tool-call `arguments` that are not a JSON object to `{}`, as Python does since vllm-project/vllm#48922. Today a malformed `arguments` string in the history (for example a call cut off at `max_tokens`) makes `/v1/chat/completions` return 500 on every later turn of the conversation.

## Claims

- The HF, DeepSeek V3.2, Inkling and `glm5_next` renderers coerce malformed and non-object `arguments` to `{}` with a warning (size only, never the content); `null` coerces without a warning, as in Python.
- A conversation whose history holds a malformed call keeps working instead of failing with 500 (400 on the render route).
- DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi K3 and Harmony keep their reference-encoding behavior.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2513 tests run: 2513 passed, 13 skipped
```

- New renderer tests for HF, DeepSeek V3.2 and Inkling cover malformed, non-object, `null` and several calls coerced independently (the cases of `tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_tool_call.py`); they fail when the helper propagates the parse failure.
- `glm5_next`: `non_object_tool_call_arguments_match_existing_hf_renderer` renders malformed, non-object, `null` and empty `arguments` with both GLM-5.3 checkpoint templates and requires the native prompt to equal the HF renderer's; it fails without the second commit.
- Replaying a call through `vllm-rs render` on the Qwen3-0.6B template over HTTP (`/v1/chat/completions/render`, no engine involved):

| `arguments` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `{"city":"Paris"}` | 200, 48 tokens | 200, 48 tokens |
| `{"cmd": "mkdir -p` | 400 `invalid JSON arguments` | 200, 44 tokens |
| `[]` | 200, 44 tokens | 200, 44 tokens |
| `42` | 200, 46 tokens (renders `42`) | 200, 44 tokens |
| `null` | 200, 44 tokens | 200, 44 tokens |

The 500 on `/v1/chat/completions` comes from the existing error mapping (`chat_template_render_failure_stays_internal`), not from a live request.

## Details

**Root cause.** A client replays assistant tool calls with `function.arguments` as the string the model produced. The Rust HF renderer decodes it and fails with `Error::ChatTemplate` when it is malformed, which is not a request-validation error, so chat returns 500. The string stays in the history, so every later turn fails the same way. DeepSeek V3.2 and Inkling fail the same way and also reject valid non-object JSON; the HF renderer passed non-object JSON through, so `42` reached the template as a number and a template calling `.items()` failed on it. Python's `_postprocess_messages` (`vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py`) coerces these to `{}` with a warning because a failure in the history makes the conversation unrecoverable.

**Design.** A shared default, `tool_call_arguments_or_empty` in the `renderer` module, decodes `arguments` to a JSON object and coerces anything else to `{}`. Each renderer opts in, because the handling differs by reference encoding:

- DeepSeek V4/V4.1 keep wrapping malformed text as `{"arguments": raw}`, as deepseek-recipe does.
- Kimi K3 keeps its raw-text block for malformed text and its error for non-object JSON.
- Harmony already renders the string verbatim.

HF's `to_template_tool_calls` can no longer fail, so it returns an `Option`.

**`glm5_next` (second commit).** Python serves `glm5_next` through the HF renderer, so these strings are coerced there too. The native Rust renderer passed the string into its template messages and its encoder rejected it with 400. The coercion now happens where the request is turned into template messages (the counterpart of Python's `parse_chat_messages`), as on the HF renderer; the encoder keeps the template's own rejection of non-object input, which `fixtures/test_cases.json` pins (`bad_arguments_*`).

**Why `{}` rather than the raw text.** HF templates need a mapping for `arguments` (`.items()`, `tojson` re-encodes a string); DeepSeek V3.2 writes DSML parameters, which a JSON string does not contain; only Inkling could carry the raw payload. The cost is one prefix-cache miss from the coerced arguments onward on the first turn that replays the call (block hashes chain); `{}` renders deterministically, so later turns hit.

**Not covered.** Warning text and counts are not asserted. Python's dict passthrough case does not apply, because the Rust request DTO carries `arguments` as a string; the empty and missing cases are already covered at the DTO by `prepare_chat_request_lowers_empty_tool_call_arguments_as_absent`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes tool-call argument handling in the Rust renderers (searched open PRs for `tool call arguments`, `malformed`, `coerce`, `glm5_next`). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Drop tool calls under tool_choice=none for split tool parsers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `tool_choice: "none"` and `tools`, drop parsed tool calls and their markup on the Rust frontend's split reasoning-plus-tool-parser path, as structured assembly already does for unified parsers. Today the raw call markup reaches `content`.

## Claims

- With `tools`, `tool_choice: "none"` and a configured tool parser (for example `qwen3_coder`, `glm47`, `kimi_k2`, `deepseek_*`, `minimax_*`), a call the model still emits is parsed and dropped: no `tool_calls`, and no markup in `content`. The surrounding content stays.
- Without a configured tool parser, the output stays plain content and no new error appears.
- `auto`, `required` and named tool choices are unchanged.

```
tools=[search], tool_choice="none", model output:
  Sure.<tool_call>\n<function=search>...</function>\n</tool_call>
before: content = "Sure.<tool_call>\n<function=search>...</tool_call>", tool_calls = []
after:  content = "Sure.",                                             tool_calls = []
```

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2510 tests run: 2510 passed, 13 skipped
```

Tests in `rust/src/chat/src/output/default/mod.rs`:

- `tool_choice_none_drops_parsed_tool_calls` runs a unified parser (gemma4), a split tool parser (qwen3_coder) and the bare-JSON Llama parser through final assembly. `auto` keeps the call each time; under `none` all three drop it (`("Sure.", [])` for gemma4 and qwen3_coder). An ordinary JSON answer stays content under both `auto` and `none`, and without a configured tool parser the markup stays content. With the fix reverted, the qwen3_coder `none` case fails with the raw markup in content.
- `answer_constraint_keeps_optional_tool_calls` asserts that `none` plus a JSON schema constrains the answer alone; it returns `None` with the fix reverted.

## Details

**Python.** `keeps_tool_calls` in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/message_assembly.py` (vllm-project/vllm#63148, vllm-project/vllm#63345) returns false for `none`, and both the non-streaming and the streaming path discard the parsed `tool_calls` while keeping `content`. The parser-engine families also strip the markup from `content`.

**Rust before this change.** Unified parsers (gemma4, kimi_k3, inkling, hf, ...) already drop the calls: `ChatRequest::max_tool_calls()` returns `Some(0)` when tool parsing is off, and structured assembly suppresses every call (vllm-project/vllm#62741). The split path (`CombinedParser`) did not: `DefaultChatOutputProcessor` built no tool parser when tool parsing was off, so the raw call markup reached `content`.

**Change.** With tools present, `DefaultChatOutputProcessor` builds the configured tool parser through one `resolve_tool_parser(&ResolvedToolContext, ..) -> Option<_>` whether tool parsing is on or off, and under `none` leaves dropping to the existing `max_tool_calls = Some(0)`. When no tool parser is configured, it keeps the existing errors with tool parsing on and returns no parser under `none`. Requests without tools still get no tool parser.

- **Layering.** The consumer of `tool_choice` here is structured assembly's `max_tool_calls`, which already serves both parser kinds; this makes parser construction in `vllm-chat`'s default output processor consistent with it. As with `auto`, a family whose parser preserves special tokens (kimi_k2, internlm2, DSML) now decodes with `skip_special_tokens=false` under `none` too, so its markers reach the parser that drops them.
- **Output grammar.** `tool_choice=none` still builds no tool grammar. With a `response_format` and no reasoning parser, the constraint now reaches the engine as a structural tag holding only that answer (`BuiltOutputGrammar::final_output_only(answer)`), the shape `CombinedParser` already builds when a tool parser is active (vllm-project/vllm#60781); it is the same constraint. Harmony is untouched.

**Differences from Python.** Rust drops the calls for every parser. Python's other parsers keep the raw call as content under `none`: the legacy non-engine tool parsers, the HF `ResponseTemplateParser` (`tests/parser/test_response_template.py::test_tool_choice_none_preserves_raw_call_as_content`), and the Llama JSON parser for bare JSON calls (`tests/parser/engine/test_llama_json.py::test_tool_choice_none_preserves_bare_json`). Under `none`, Rust's `llama3_json`/`llama4_json` parse a bare JSON object naming a tool as a call and drop it; other JSON stays content. OpenAI's `tool_choice: "none"` means the model does not call tools, so surfacing calls or their raw markup is wrong either way.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes tool-call handling under `tool_choice: "none"` in the Rust frontend (searched open Rust frontend PRs for `tool_choice` and tool parser construction). vllm-project/vllm#63580 maps `ParserDisabled` to a 400 for requests with tool parsing on; it is orthogonal, since this change keeps that error where it is raised today. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept FastAPI boolean spellings on dev route query parameters
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Accept FastAPI's boolean spellings on the Rust frontend's dev and RL route query parameters, so `requests.post(f"{url}/pause", params={"clear_cache": True})` works as it does against the Python frontend instead of returning 400.

## Claims

- `clear_cache` on `/pause`, `reset_running_requests` and `reset_external` on `/reset_prefix_cache`, and `include_dp` on `/get_world_size` accept `true`/`t`/`yes`/`y`/`on`/`1` and `false`/`f`/`no`/`n`/`off`/`0`, case-insensitively, like FastAPI.
- Any other value is still rejected with 400.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2514 tests run: 2514 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `query_bool_matches_fastapi_spellings` (`vllm-server` `utils`): a table of 41 values, probed against a live FastAPI app rather than taken from the docs, with their parsed value or rejection.
- `pause_route_accepts_python_spelled_bool_query_value`, `reset_prefix_cache_route_accepts_python_spelled_bool_query_values`, `world_size_route_accepts_python_spelled_bool_query_value`: route tests against the scripted mock engine, asserting the utility-call arguments the engine receives.
- With the routes back on plain `bool`, the four tests fail (the route tests with 400 instead of 200, the table test on `True`).
- No real model or live server was run; the change is limited to query parsing.

## Details

**Root cause.** The Python routes declare these parameters as `bool` query parameters, which FastAPI parses with pydantic's lenient coercion. The Rust routes declared them as plain `bool` under axum's `Query`, and serde only takes lowercase `true` and `false`. `requests` encodes Python's `True` with `str()`, i.e. `True`, so a call that works on Python gets a 400 on Rust. Python's own RL test helpers send exactly this (`tests/entrypoints/rl/conftest.py`: `pause(..., clear_cache=...)`, `get_world_size(..., include_dp=...)`). `httpx` sends lowercase and is not affected.

**Change.** One `deserialize_query_bool` in `vllm-server`'s `utils`, next to `utility_call_error` which the same handlers already use, applied to the four fields of `PauseParams`, `ResetPrefixCacheParams` and `WorldSizeParams`. Nothing below the routes changes. These are the only boolean query parameters on routes the Rust frontend serves.

**Why only query parameters.** JSON request bodies are typed: clients encode a boolean as `true`/`false`, so pydantic's leniency there (accepting `"True"`, `"yes"`, `1` for a `bool` field) is never exercised by a real client, and the Rust bodies stay strict. A query string is untyped text whose spelling is chosen by the client library, which is where the difference shows up.

**Behavior left as is.**

- An invalid value is a 400 on Rust and a 422 on Python, as for other invalid query values.
- `/pause` reports `param: "mode"` for every query error, now including an invalid `clear_cache`; this mapping predates the PR.
- A repeated key (`?a=1&a=0`) is a 400 on Rust; Python takes the last value.

**Python tests.** `tests/entrypoints/rl/state_transitions/test_pause_resume.py` pins `clear_cache=True` and `False`, but its fixture launches `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server`, which never delegates to the Rust frontend, so it cannot cover this path without a fixture change, which is out of scope here.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes query parsing on the Rust dev routes (searched open PRs for `clear_cache`, `query bool`, `boolean query`, `reset_prefix_cache`). vllm-project/vllm#64900 adds a `preserve_running_requests` query parameter on the Python side only; it does not overlap. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust][Benchmark] Map --output-len to the sharegpt and hf datasets
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64939.

`--output-len` is silently ignored for `--dataset-name sharegpt` and `hf` in the Rust `vllm-bench`: each request's output length comes from the dataset's reference answer instead. Python `vllm bench serve` maps the flag onto both datasets, and Rust already does so for random, custom and prefix_repetition.

This PR:

- Maps `--output-len` onto `sharegpt_output_len` and `hf_output_len`. It takes precedence over the dataset-specific flags, matching Python and the other Rust datasets. Runs that don't pass `--output-len` are unchanged.
- Extends the existing hf check so `--output-len 0` is rejected for `--dataset-name hf`, as `--hf-output-len 0` already is. `--output-len 0` on other datasets isn't affected by this check.
- Updates the `--output-len` help text to say what it maps to.

`--multi-turn` reads the same two config fields, so ShareGPT multi-turn runs now honor `--output-len` as well.

SPEED-Bench is left alone: `--output-len` isn't mapped to `--speed-bench-output-len` in Python either. The question about its README examples is in the issue.

## Not a duplicate

I found no open issue or PR covering this. #62477 changes how output tokens are counted, not the requested length.

## Test Plan

New tests in `config::tests`:
- `test_output_len_maps_to_sharegpt_and_hf`: no flag gives `None`, each flag works alone, and `--output-len` wins when both are set. It fails without the mapping change.
- `test_hf_rejects_zero_output_len`: `--output-len 0` and `--hf-output-len 0` are both rejected.

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-bench
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

End-to-end against a mock OpenAI-compatible server that logs each request's `max_completion_tokens`, 20 prompts, `--backend openai-chat`.

## Test Result

- `cargo test -p vllm-bench`: all pass (217 unit tests and 3 CLI parity tests). Clippy and fmt are clean.

| Dataset and flags | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| sharegpt `--output-len 32` | 8 to 600 (3080 tokens) | 32 on all (640 tokens) |
| hf (`openai/gsm8k`) `--output-len 32` | 47 to 199 (2394 tokens) | 32 on all (640 tokens) |
| sharegpt `--multi-turn --output-len 32` | 8 to 600 | 32 on all |
| sharegpt, no flag | 8 to 600 | 8 to 600 (unchanged) |
| sharegpt `--output-len 32 --sharegpt-output-len 16` | not run | 32 on all |
| random `--output-len 32` | not run | 32 on all |

The Python client with sharegpt `--output-len 32` sends 32 on all requests (640 tokens), matching the new behavior.

AI assistance: prepared with Claude Code; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above locally.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Return 501 for /generative_scoring and the opt-in Cohere v2 chat routes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Return 501 instead of a bare 404 from the Rust frontend for two Python routes it does not implement: `POST /generative_scoring`, and the opt-in Cohere v2 routes `POST /cohere/v2/chat` and `POST /cohere/v2/chat/render`, under the same gates as Python. A preparatory commit replaces the router builder's positional boolean gates with a small struct.

## Claims

- `POST /generative_scoring` returns 501 with the shared "not supported by the Rust frontend yet" error instead of 404. Python registers the route for every generate model with no flag, so the placeholder has no gate either.
- With `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=1`, `POST /cohere/v2/chat` returns 501; `POST /cohere/v2/chat/render` returns 501 only when `--enable-scale-out` is also set. Without the opt-in both stay 404, as in Python.
- The `RouteGates` refactor does not change behavior.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2511 tests run: 2511 passed, 13 skipped
```

Tests in `rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs`:

- `unimplemented_python_routes_return_not_implemented` now includes `/generative_scoring`; it fails without the route (404 instead of 501).
- `cohere_routes_follow_the_python_gates` covers all three gate combinations; it fails with the env gate removed (501 instead of 404 when disabled) and with the scale-out gate removed.

## Details

One commit per change:

1. **`POST /generative_scoring`.** Python registers it in `register_generate_api_routers` (`vllm/entrypoints/generate/api_router.py`, router in `vllm/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/api_router.py`). The Rust router had no route, so a client got a 404 that reads like a wrong URL rather than a missing feature. It now uses the shared `not_supported` handler, next to the other unimplemented Python routes (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/decisions`, ...).
2. **Route gates as one struct (no behavior change).** `build_router_with_options` took three positional booleans (dev mode, runtime LoRA updating, scale-out), and test-only wrappers forwarded fixed values to it. The gates are now a private `RouteGates` struct resolved once in `build_router`; tests build the router with the gates they need (`..RouteGates::default()`).
3. **Cohere v2 chat routes.** Python's `attach_router` (`vllm/entrypoints/cohere/api_router.py`) registers chat under `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API`, and render only when scale-out (or `--tokens-only`) is also on. On the Rust frontend that opt-in did nothing. A new `RouteGates::cohere_api` gate, read next to its neighbors in `build_router`, registers both routes with `not_supported` under the same conditions. `--tokens-only` fails startup on the Rust frontend, so `--enable-scale-out` is the whole scale-out condition.

**Differences from Python.**

- Python also needs the optional `cohere` SDK and otherwise logs a warning and registers nothing. The Rust frontend has no such dependency, and a 501 tells an operator who asked for the API more than a 404 would.
- The 501 uses the shared error shape rather than Python's Cohere error envelope, like the other placeholders.
- The Cohere test passes the gates directly rather than through `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API`, like the sibling dev-mode and runtime-LoRA gates; the crate has no env-isolated test harness.

Not a duplicate: vllm-project/vllm#46427 implements `/generative_scoring` in Rust but has been inactive since 2026-10-07; this placeholder does not block it. No open PR adds the Cohere routes to the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for Rust frontend generative scoring and Cohere). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Omit unset usage prompt_tokens_details and message annotations like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Leave unset `usage.prompt_tokens_details` and `choices[].message.annotations` out of Rust frontend responses instead of sending them as `null`, matching the Python frontend since vllm-project/vllm#64177 (issue vllm-project/vllm#61425). The OpenAI spec types both as optional but not nullable, and strict schema validators reject the `null`.

## Claims

- `usage.prompt_tokens_details` is omitted when `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` is off, on every route that reports usage (chat, completions, generate; streamed or not). With the flag on, it is reported unchanged.
- `choices[].message.annotations` is omitted on non-streaming chat completions. The Rust frontend never produces annotations, so the key is always absent.
- Other unset fields keep their explicit `null`, including `completion_tokens_details` (Python also still sends `null` there).

Before (Rust), after this PR both keys are absent:

```
"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi","refusal":null,"annotations":null,"audio":null,"function_call":null,"reasoning":null}
"usage":{"prompt_tokens":22,"total_tokens":25,"completion_tokens":3,"prompt_tokens_details":null,"completion_tokens_details":null}
```

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2510 tests run: 2510 passed, 13 skipped
```

- Red-green: removing either attribute makes its tests fail (`usage_tests::token_usage_hides_prompt_token_details_by_default`, `routes::tests::non_stream_chat_returns_json_response`, `routes::tests::non_stream_completions_return_json_response`).
- Each commit on its own: workspace clippy clean and `vllm-server` tests pass.

## Details

One commit per field:

1. **`usage.prompt_tokens_details`**: `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on `Usage::prompt_tokens_details` (`routes/openai/utils/types.rs`). `Usage` is the single wire type that chat, completions and generate report, streamed or not, mirroring Python's single `UsageInfo`; the field-level attribute is where Python's `exclude_if` sits, so every route and stream mode follows one rule.
2. **`message.annotations`**: the same attribute on `ChatCompletionMessage::annotations` (`routes/openai/chat_completions/types.rs`), the non-streaming chat message wire type. Python's typing change to `list[...]` has no wire effect while the value is always unset.

Python consistency: `prompt_tokens_details` is omitted on every Python route and in both stream modes (field-level `exclude_if`; stream chunks already drop it), and `annotations` exists only on the non-streaming chat message. The OpenAI SDK parses responses without either key.

Not changed: an unset `completion_tokens_details` on stream chunks. Python drops it on the usage-only final chunk (`exclude_none`) and on completions continuous-usage chunks (`exclude_unset`), but sends `null` on its own chat and generate continuous-usage chunks; matching that needs a usage representation that depends on the chunk kind, so it is left for a separate change.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes these fields in the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for `prompt_tokens_details`, `annotations` and Rust frontend usage; vllm-project/vllm#60624 adds `multimodal_tokens` and vllm-project/vllm#64573 is a Python change). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Include error sources in HTTP 400 messages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's HTTP 400 responses drop the source chain of request validation errors. A request pinned with `X-data-parallel-rank` to a rank the frontend does not own returns only `"engine-core error"`, hiding which ranks are connected. Related: vllm-project/vllm#64801.

## Claims

- HTTP 400 validation errors from `text_submit_error` / `chat_submit_error` include the full error report, matching the 500 branch and the gRPC path (`text_error_to_status`).
- Hyper connection errors in the trace log include their source chain.
- No other validation error message changes: `InvalidDataParallelRank` is the only one wrapped by a non-transparent layer.

## Validation

New test `chat_completions_unconnected_data_parallel_rank_reports_connected_ranks` mirrors the existing gRPC test `unary_generate_unconnected_data_parallel_rank_returns_invalid_argument`. It connects a mock engine at global rank 3 and pins the request to rank 0.

| | `error.message` |
| --- | --- |
| Before (test fails) | `engine-core error` |
| After | `engine-core error: data parallel rank 0 is not connected to this frontend; connected ranks: [3]` |

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server`: 553 passed, including the existing `error::tests` that pin other 400 messages.
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Details

`text_submit_error` and `chat_submit_error` formatted 400 messages with `"{error}"` (`Display`), while their 500 branch uses `to_report_string()`. The data-parallel rank error reaches them as `vllm_chat::Error::Text` → `vllm_text::Error::Llm` → `vllm_llm::Error::EngineCoreClient` → `InvalidDataParallelRank`. The first two layers are transparent, but `EngineCoreClient` is `#[error("engine-core error")]`, so `Display` stops there and the rank detail lives only in `source()`.

For the trace log: hyper 1.x prints only the error kind in `Display` (e.g. "connection error") and keeps the underlying I/O error in `source()`.

Other error formatting sites in production code were audited. The remaining `Display` uses format leaf errors (serde, I/O, join, parse errors), or types whose `Display` already embeds the inner error.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DeepEP] Upgrade to 2.1 and retain per-context GIN completion ordering
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Upgrade vendored DeepEP to 2.1 (`a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8`), which includes the upstream NVLink visibility fix, and retain a smaller patch for per-context GIN completion signaling.

## Claims

- Use upstream flush, NVLink fence, and grid synchronization placement; remove the custom deferred-flush implementation. Completion signals cover every allocated context, while arrival-only barriers use context 0.
- Retain the nine-context allocation for vLLM's direct-mode MoE buffers, matching automatic active-QP selection. Hybrid allocation stays automatic.
- Preserve skipped/already-applied/failed patch diagnostics requested in review, including aborting on failed application. Add the NCCL library search path required by DeepEP 2.1's SONAME linking and document runtime-version requirements.

## Validation

**Current revision: build and offline checks pass. Distributed correctness, model execution, and overhead remain unvalidated on this revision.** GPU attempts were blocked by unavailable capacity and RDMA device admission failures (`no healthy devices present ... rdma/ib`); these are infrastructure failures, not correctness results. Earlier performance numbers do not apply to this upgrade, so this description makes no overhead claim.

| Current-revision check | Result |
|---|---|
| Fresh native wheels, CUDA 13 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / SM90 | Built against NCCL 2.30.7 and 2.31.2 |
| Patched world/rail barrier templates, completion and arrival variants | Compiled with nvcc against both NCCL versions |
| Linux patch application, byte-exact header, complete reverse dry-run | Passed; patched header SHA256 `1bc42abd841cc6e9ba6c59b68962d7e260e163a750873bd50633f91e89d0979f` |
| Native import and loaded-NCCL provenance | Passed on two H200 workers with NCCL 2.30.7; distributed operation did not start |
| Installer behavior | Seven paths passed: fresh, already applied, partial, wrong ref, broken patch, missing patch, other project |
| NCCL linker-path selection | Passed for explicit EP root, legacy root, pip metadata, missing installation |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed |

Build checks used `uv build --wheel --no-build-isolation` with `EP_NUM_TOPK_IDX_BITS=64`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0`, and explicit matching NCCL roots. Patch checks used `patch --batch -p1` and `patch --batch --force --reverse --dry-run -p1`. Local validation artifacts retain the source, wheel, NCCL, and resulting-header hashes.

```bash
pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json \
  docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md \
  tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh \
  tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch
```

Before merge, rerun matched EP8 direct-mode stock/patched correctness at 9/17 contexts, representative direct/hybrid operator timings, and the original vLLM model reproducer on this revision. Ordinary CI does not cover the three-node H200/GDAKI reproducer.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence on the previous DeepEP pin — not validation of this upgrade</summary>

The previous `d4f41e4e` implementation at PR commit `c781de2f82` passed the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash reproducer: DP8/TP1/EP, three H200 nodes (4+2+2), NCCL 2.30.7, direct `deepep_v2`, eager execution. Six rounds of 64 requests completed (384/384); all eight audit ranks saved checkpoints and all three servers exited 0, with no count/slot mismatches, barrier timeouts, or illegal memory accesses. The audit run was not a serving-performance comparison.

The old pristine pin and per-context-only variant had previously faulted. Subsequent isolated controls also reproduced old-pin correctness failures before graph capture/profiling. These results concern the old pin with direct mode explicitly forced; they do not establish that default hybrid deployments are affected or that stock DeepEP 2.1 fails.

</details>

## Details

GIN ordering is per context ([NVIDIA/nccl#2302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/2302)); a completion signal on context 0 alone does not supply ordering for puts on other contexts. The selected upstream revision already contains the NVLink visibility fence from [DeepEP#715](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/715). The remaining vendor patch signals and waits on each context at data completion, retaining upstream flush/fence placement and adding context information to timeout diagnostics.

The pin also includes runtime-sized NCCL DevComm compatibility and strict-ordering window registration. Builds against NCCL <2.31 require the same runtime NCCL version. Both tested NCCL configurations used rebuilt native extensions. The constructor/combine signatures are unchanged, and dispatch's new optional argument is compatible with vLLM's keyword calls. DeepEP 2.5 removes the ElasticBuffer and legacy APIs used by vLLM, so that broader migration is outside this fix.

This updates the existing PR rather than creating a duplicate. AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, validation, and this description. The human submitter must review all changed lines and the validation evidence.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Model] Fill the model info cache once in the model init and tensor schema tests
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add `ModelRegistry.fill_model_info_cache()`, which inspects every lazily registered model that is missing from the model info cache in one subprocess, and call it once per module in `tests/models/test_initialization.py` and `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py`. Today every case in those modules pays a ~10 s cache miss. Related: #23558 (added the cache), #51746 (closed; proposed a CLI to pre-fill it).

## Claims

- One fill of all 418 registered architectures takes 17.4 s; after it, each case reads the cache. Per case, `EngineArgs.create_engine_config` drops from a median of 10.3 s to 0.4 s in the init test, and `ModelConfig(...)` from 11.9 s to 1-2 s in the tensor schema test.
- Same cases, same results, less time on MI300X: 16 init cases 516 s -> 352 s (-32%), 14 tensor schema cases 335 s -> 211 s (-37%).
- Expected CI saving, at the last 7 days' run rate of main plus PR builds: about 155 machine-hours a day across (MI355 DPX) Basic Models (Extra Initialization), Multimodal Processor and Basic Models (Initialization). NVIDIA and XPU jobs running these modules pay the same miss today.
- No behavior change outside callers of the new method: `inspect_model_cls` is unchanged apart from moving its module hash lookup into `_get_module_hash()`.

## Validation

Environment: CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a19b0e-d62f-4889-8556-b5c2d4478cbf` (vllm/ci build 99098) with this PR applied as a patch, one MI300X, every run from an empty `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` as in CI. One run per row (n=1) on a shared machine, so absolute times are inflated and variability was not measured.

Commands run:

```bash
pytest -q models/test_registry.py -k "fill_model_info_cache or lazy_modelinfo"
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d) python -c "from vllm import ModelRegistry; ModelRegistry.fill_model_info_cache()"
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
pytest -v -s models/test_initialization.py -k "test_can_initialize_large_subset and (HfMoondream or PhiForCausalLM or Zamba2ForCausalLM or BertModel or GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM or Blip2ForConditionalGeneration or Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration or DeciLMForCausalLM or WhisperForConditionalGeneration or AfmoeForCausalLM or Rnj1ForCausalLM or DeepseekV32MTPModel)"
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
pytest -v -s models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k "InternVL3-1B-hf or Qwen2-Audio-7B or Qwen2-VL-2B or deepseek-vl2-tiny or pixtral-12b or whisper-large-v3 or Kimi-VL-A3B-Thinking or Qwen2.5-VL-3B or MiniCPM-o-2_6 or Molmo-7B-O-0924 or canary-1b-v2"
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py
```

| Command | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| registry tests (new `test_fill_model_info_cache`, 2 existing cache tests, 2 `test_registry_inspect_does_not_init_cuda`) | - | 5 passed |
| `fill_model_info_cache()` from an empty cache | - | 17.4 s, 346 cache entries |
| caller after `fill_model_info_cache()`: CUDA initialized / new vLLM modules imported | - | no / 0 |
| batch entries vs the same batch in reversed import order | - | 346 of 346 identical |
| batch entries vs the existing per-model `inspect_model_cls` path, 15 random models | - | identical |
| init sample | 14 passed, 2 skipped in 516.11s | 14 passed, 2 skipped in 351.76s |
| tensor schema sample | 12 passed, 2 skipped in 334.85s | 12 passed, 2 skipped in 211.28s |
| pre-commit | - | all hooks passed |

The per-case medians in Claims come from a copy of the test that timestamps each phase. This PR was also run together with #65442: both modules passed.

CI coverage: the new unit test runs with `tests/models/test_registry.py` in Basic Models (Other); the changed modules run in Basic Models (Initialization), Basic Models (Extra Initialization) and Multimodal Processor on NVIDIA and their AMD mirrors, and in the Intel XPU jobs. No model output changes, so no model evaluation applies.

## Details

- Root cause: on a miss, `_LazyRegisteredModel.inspect_model_cls` imports and inspects the model class in a fresh subprocess (to keep CUDA out of the caller), then writes `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/modelinfos`. CI jobs start with an empty `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`, and these modules test each architecture once, so every case missed.
- `fill_model_info_cache()` runs one `_run_in_subprocess` call that, for every lazily registered model whose cache entry is missing or stale, inspects the model and writes the result with the existing `_save_modelinfo_to_cache`. Entries are keyed by the model file hash exactly as `inspect_model_cls` keys them.
- The cache lookup runs in the subprocess too: resolving a module outside `vllm/model_executor/models` (the `vllm.models.*` packages) imports its package, and some of those import model code that initializes CUDA. A first version looked up the cache in the caller; in the CI image that initialized CUDA in the caller, which would break fork-based NVIDIA runs. With the lookup in the subprocess, the caller imports no new vLLM modules and leaves CUDA uninitialized (checked).
- Best effort: a model that fails to inspect in the batch (3 of 418 on ROCm: `Terratorch` needs an uninstalled package, `Dots3NoteForCausalLM` and `Dots3NoteMTPModel` import CUDA-only flash attention) gets no entry and is inspected by `inspect_model_cls` as before, so its error still surfaces in its own case. If the subprocess fails as a whole, the method logs a warning and returns.
- The calling process imports no model modules, so fork-based NVIDIA runs are unaffected.
- Tradeoff: about 17 s per module per job, even when a job runs one case from the module (the Intel job that runs a single `test_can_initialize_large_subset` case). With a warm cache the call still starts one subprocess (about 10 s) to check it.
- Docs: the method is documented by its docstring, which the API reference renders; no user-facing behavior changes.
- Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for "model info cache", "modelinfos" and "inspect_model_cls subprocess". The only related open PR, #57311, moves `atomic_writer` out of `weight_utils` and does not change when the cache is filled. #51746 proposed a `vllm prepare-model-info` command and was closed.
- AI assistance: this change and this description were prepared with an AI coding assistant (Cursor). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align speculator hidden norm in GLM-4.5/4.6 MoE and GLM-OCR MTP with GLM5Next to recycle post-final-hidden.
commits.pr_body:
### Overview

Three GLM-family MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) models — `glm4_moe_mtp.py` (GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.5-Air / GLM-4.6), `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` (GLM-4.7-Flash), and `glm_ocr_mtp.py` (GLM-OCR) — return the **pre-final-norm** hidden from the MTP layer, so the speculator recycles a hidden that is one RMSNorm short into the next draft step's `hnorm`. The established GLM/DeepSeek-NextN contract (already merged in vLLM by #47448 and also SGLang's `glm4_moe_nextn`/`deepseek_nextn` `vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`) recycles the **post-final-norm** hidden. This PR extends that contract to the three models it missed, and registers them in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` so Model Runner V1 unpacks the new tuple return. Draft-only change; verified output is unaffected.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Real-object drafter test and an e2e test on both model runners (GLM-OCR) in CI; acceptance validated out-of-CI on GLM-4.5-Air (checkpoint too large for CI).
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

commits.pr_title: [Rust][Benchmark] Record ramp-up runs in the result JSON and filename
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64226.

With `--ramp-up-strategy`, the Rust `vllm-bench` sends requests on the ramp-up schedule but saves the result as if it were a fixed-rate run: the file is named `<label>-infqps-...json`, and the result JSON has no ramp-up information, so it can't be told apart from a burst run. `--request-rate` given alongside ramp-up is ignored by the schedule but still ends up in the filename and `request_rate`.

This PR matches Python `vllm bench serve`:

- **Filename** (`compute_result_filename`): `<label>-ramp-up-<strategy>-<start>qps-<end>qps[-concurrencyN]-<model>-<dt>.json`.
- **Result JSON** (`build_result_json`): `ramp_up_strategy`, `ramp_up_start_rps`, `ramp_up_end_rps`.
- **`rps_change_events`**: the start rate, then every integer RPS reached, each with the local timestamp of the first request sent at that rate. Python records these in its dispatch generator. Here the schedule is precomputed, so `RequestSchedule::rps_change_offsets` derives them from the per-request `rates` that `compute_schedule` already returned (previously `#[allow(dead_code)]`), offset from the benchmark start.
- **Validation** (`parse_ramp_up`): reject `--request-rate` and `--sweep-request-rate` with ramp-up, and a start RPS above the end RPS, as Python does. Same reasoning as the existing self-timed check in `config.rs`: a rate that never ran shouldn't label the result.

One difference from Python remains: Python parses the ramp-up RPS as `int`, while the Rust CLI takes `f64`, so the JSON has `2.0` where Python has `2`. Both parse to the same number; the filename is identical (`2qps`).

## Not a duplicate

No open issue or PR covers Rust bench ramp-up results or `rps_change_events`. #42427 changes Python ramp-up validation only.

## Test Plan

New tests:
- `config::tests::test_ramp_up_result_filename`: ramp-up config with `--max-concurrency 8` gives `openai-ramp-up-linear-2qps-10qps-concurrency8-model-<dt>.json`.
- `config::tests::test_ramp_up_rejects_request_rate_flags`: `--request-rate` and `--sweep-request-rate` are rejected with ramp-up.
- `config::tests::test_ramp_up_rejects_start_above_end`.
- `output::json::tests::test_insert_ramp_up`: the three ramp-up fields.
- `rate_control::tests::test_rps_change_offsets`: start rate at 0, one step per integer rate, and rates a single request jumps over share its delay.

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

End-to-end, same mock OpenAI-compatible server for both clients: `--backend openai --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 4 --num-prompts 40 --ramp-up-strategy linear --ramp-up-start-rps 2 --ramp-up-end-rps 10 --save-result`.

## Test Result

- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib`: 209 passed. Clippy and fmt are clean.

End-to-end:

| | Python | Rust, before | Rust, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| filename | `openai-ramp-up-linear-2qps-10qps-...` | `openai-infqps-...` | `openai-ramp-up-linear-2qps-10qps-...` |
| `ramp_up_strategy` / `_start_rps` / `_end_rps` | `linear` / `2` / `10` | missing | `linear` / `2.0` / `10.0` |
| `rps_change_events` (rps) | 2, 3, …, 10 | missing | 2, 3, …, 10 |
| `--request-rate 5` with ramp-up | `ValueError` | runs, saves `openai-5qps-...` | config error |
| start RPS 10, end RPS 2 | `ValueError` | runs | config error |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Reject --dataset-path with synthetic vllm-bench datasets
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #64538. Rust `vllm-bench` silently ignored `--dataset-path` for the synthetic datasets, so `vllm-bench --dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` without `--dataset-name` benchmarked random prompts instead of the given file. This rejects the combination with the same error as Python `vllm bench serve`.

## Claims

- `--dataset-path` with `random`, `random-mm`, `random-rerank` or `prefix_repetition` (including the default `--dataset-name random`) now fails at startup with Python's error: `Cannot use '<name>' dataset with --dataset-path. Please specify the appropriate --dataset-name (e.g., 'sharegpt', 'custom', 'hf') for your dataset file: <path>`.
- Datasets that read `--dataset-path` (`sharegpt`, `speed-bench`, `hf`, `custom`, `timed_trace`) are unchanged.
- `--dataset-path` help text and the bench README document the restriction.

## Validation

Regression tests in `config.rs`: `test_synthetic_dataset_rejects_dataset_path` and `test_default_dataset_rejects_dataset_path` fail without the fix and pass with it; `test_file_dataset_accepts_dataset_path` passes in both.

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-bench                                   # all pass
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings    # clean
cargo fmt -p vllm-bench --check                            # clean
```

End-to-end, release build against a mock OpenAI-compatible server that logs received prompts. `my_workload.jsonl` holds 5 lines of `{"prompt": "MY_REAL_WORKLOAD_PROMPT", "output_tokens": 4}`; common args `--model mock-model --tokenizer gpt2 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --num-prompts 5`.

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` | exit 0, "5 random prompts"; `MY_REAL_WORKLOAD_PROMPT` received 0 times | exit 1: `Cannot use 'random' dataset with --dataset-path ...` |
| `--dataset-path /no/such/file.jsonl` | exit 0 | exit 1, same error |
| `--dataset-name random-rerank --backend vllm-rerank --dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` | — | exit 1: `Cannot use 'random-rerank' dataset ...` |
| `--dataset-name custom --dataset-path my_workload.jsonl` | — | exit 0; `MY_REAL_WORKLOAD_PROMPT` received 5/5 times |
| `--dataset-name random` (no path) | — | exit 0 |
| `vllm bench serve` (Python), first row's command | exit 1, same error | unchanged |

The same error is returned with `--multi-turn`, `--sweep-max-concurrency` and `--num-runs`. `mm-processor` has no `--dataset-path` flag and already rejects it as an unexpected argument.

## Details

- **Root cause:** Python checks this combination in `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`; the Rust port never did, and none of the four synthetic generators read `dataset_path`. Since `--dataset-name` defaults to `random`, a forgotten `--dataset-name` produced plausible-looking results for the wrong workload.
- **Placement:** the check is in `BenchConfig::from_args`, next to the other per-dataset validation. Every serve mode (single run, multi-turn, sweeps, `--num-runs`) builds its config there, so one check covers all of them.
- **Parity:** same dataset list and message as Python. The dataset name in the message comes from the CLI value (`ValueEnum::to_possible_value`), so it matches what the user typed.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open or closed PR or issue covers this; I searched for `64538`, "dataset-path", "vllm-bench dataset-path", and "Cannot use dataset with --dataset-path" before opening #64538 and this PR.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Muse Spark Open Specialized Decode: Optimized GB300 Decode (1.5x)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This is an NVIDIA-developed specialized decode of Muse Spark Open (NVFP4, DSpark speculative decoding) for GB300 that gives 1.5x single-stream decode throughput, in the form of the Kimi K3 specialized decode (#61867). - Tensor parallel 4, 8 or 16 with expert parallelism (EP = TP); at TP8 the routed experts run tensor-parallel inside the executor. - DSpark verification with 7 draft tokens, including the draft model's forward and its Markov sampling loop. - Any context length up to `--max-model-len`, including sliding-window layers. It is opt-in with `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`; the default, `auto`, keeps the stock decode. Changes are localized to `vllm/models/muse_spark/` (the executor in `nvidia/specialized_decode/`, the model hooks, and the DSpark draft model, which implements the speculator's `sample_sequential` hook) plus three CUDA C ops in `csrc/muse_spark/` and their registration (`CMakeLists.txt`, `csrc/ops.h`, `csrc/torch_bindings.cpp`, `vllm/_custom_ops.py`, additions only). No other shared vLLM code changes. ## Claims Single-stream decode (ISL 1, OSL 1000, concurrency 1, DSpark K 7 with forced acceptance length 6) on GB300 NVL72 trays, ours and stock vLLM on one allocation per row: - **TP8+EP8: 1.53x** (698.60 -> 1072.14 tok/s/user) - **gsm8k matches stock** within one standard error at TP8+EP8 (1253 vs 1255 of 1319). ## Validation ### Correctness Testing | Task | Stock TP8+EP8 | Ours TP8+EP8 | |---|---|---| | gsm8k 5-shot, flexible-extract (n 1319) | 0.9515 +- 0.0059 | 0.9500 +- 0.0060 | | gsm8k 5-shot, strict-match (n 1319) | 0.9522 +- 0.0059 | 0.9492 +- 0.0060 | `--max-model-len 32768`, adaptive verification off, block rejection, concurrency 1, both arms on one allocation. Paired, U - S is -2 questions (flexible-extract; exact McNemar p 0.83). Greedy outputs at TP4, TP8 and TP16 are identical across server starts. **Accuracy** (TP=4, single concurrency, real rejection sampling, max-model-len 32768) | Dataset | Original decode | Dedicated decode | |---|---|---| | OCRBench (1000 questions) | 81.8 | 81.6 | | AIME26 (30 questions, temperature 1.0) | 93.3% (28/30) | 93.3% (28/30) | ### Performance Validation DSpark speculative decoding only (the executor serves the verify step); median interactivity (1000 / median TPOT) over 200 requests, each row's two arms on one allocation.
Commands and setup ```bash # Server: each tray runs one vllm serve with --node-rank k (rank 0 serves the API, the others add --headless) vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size <8|16> --enable-expert-parallel --nnodes <2|4> --node-rank --master-addr \ --max-model-len <2048|1048576> --reasoning-parser muse --tool-call-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"","num_speculative_tokens":7, "draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length":6,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' # ours only # Client vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1000 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --seed 0 \ --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 200 --num-warmups 2 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el ``` Both arms: vLLM main at 1fd6337e22 (stock) and the same with this change, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (vLLM's pin), the model with its two BF16 expert layers quantized to NVFP4 locally, no `--linear-backend`, the default FlashInfer all-reduce backend.
## Details ### vLLM Integration The Muse Spark model builds a `SpecializedDecode` after its weights load (`nvidia/model_state.py`, using the ModelState protocol and `initialize_kv_cache()` as #61867 does) and calls it from `forward()`. It serves the verify step of one request (1 + 7 draft tokens) captured into FULL CUDA graphs; when `plan()` returns None (prefill, mixed batches, several requests, partial drafts, eager or PIECEWISE steps) the stock forward runs. `unsupported()` checks the deployment at startup and names the first requirement it fails. The lm_head, `compute_logits` and the attention backend's metadata and KV cache stay shared. The executor runs, per layer, the input boundary, the attention (fused QKV + QK-norm + RoPE + KV insert, decode attention fused with the output norm and gate, o_proj), the attention boundary and the MoE (FP32 router, routing that also writes the routed experts' metadata, pooler GEMM with a fused all-gather + norm + NVFP4 quantization, the TRT-LLM-gen routed experts, finalize, unpooler GEMM), each block a provider in `specialized_decode/runtime/`. The fused all-reduce boundaries sum in the order of the stock FlashInfer all-reduce backend the deployment resolves (MNNVL or TRT-LLM), so TP4 needs vLLM's FlashInfer all-reduce. The draft model runs its forward and, through the DSpark speculator's `sample_sequential` hook, the Markov loop over a vocab-parallel Markov head (`runtime/draft.py`, `runtime/markov.py`). Kernels are in `specialized_decode/cutedsl/` (CuTe DSL) and `csrc/muse_spark/` (CUDA C: the QKV front, the decode attention and the routing). FlashInfer is used only from `runtime/flashinfer_ops.py`: the public routed experts ops, and on NVFP4 layers the runner below the public op, fed by the package's routing metadata, with the expert-TP tactic pinned per trtllm-gen cubin package (the op's default under any other). Kernels that reuse FlashInfer code are adapted from its source at a public sha, each header carrying the Apache-2.0 notice. Unit and kernel tests are kept out of this PR, as in #61867 (available on request; 2735 passed on one GB300 tray).
