commits.pr_title: [ROCm] [RDNA] [Perf] Add tuned configs for TRITON_ATTN kernel and swap places of TRITON_ATTN and ROCM_ATTN in priority list
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On gfx1201 (RDNA4) and gfx1100 (RDNA3), swap `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN` in vLLM's attention-backend priority list, so `TRITON_ATTN` becomes the default. This PR also adds launch configs for `TRITON_ATTN` on both GPUs, tuned with synthetic sweeps. With them, `TRITON_ATTN` is faster than `ROCM_ATTN` overall, including where `ROCM_ATTN` uses its HIP paged-attention decode kernel. The same configs are used with an fp8 KV cache.

This PR includes #60658 (closed), which had the launch configs only.

## Changes

**`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`:**
- `get_valid_backends()`, on gfx1201 and gfx1100: `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN` swap places in the priority list. Nothing else moves.
  - **Exception:** an `fp8_e5m2` KV cache keeps `ROCM_ATTN`. `Attention` quantizes the query to fp8 only for `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` caches, and rejects `fp8_e5m2` for backends that take an fp8 query, as `TRITON_ATTN` does on gfx1201.
  - **Unchanged:** an explicit `--attention-backend`, and every other GPU (including gfx1200, gfx1101 and gfx1151).
- New `on_gfx1201()` helper.

**`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`:** only launch parameters change (`BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_Q`, `TILE_SIZE`, `num_warps`, `num_stages`, split-KV segments) and, on gfx1201, the 2D/3D decode threshold. The kernels themselves are untouched.

How the configs are applied:
- They're looked up by the padded head size (`next_power_of_2`): head 96 uses the 128 configs, 192 the 256 configs.
- They apply to every attention variant (sliding window, sinks, softcap, ALiBi), because those are applied per element inside each tile.
- Batch-invariant mode keeps the default launch.

*gfx1201:*
- **Prefill / chunked / mixed** (`max_seqlen_q > 64`, GQA ≤ 16), as (`BLOCK_M`, `TILE`, warps, stages):

  | head_size | 64 < max_seqlen_q < 4096 | max_seqlen_q ≥ 4096 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 64 | 64, 64, 4, 1 | 128, 64, 8, 1 |
  | 128 | 64, 32, 4, 1 | 128, 32, 8, 2 |
  | 256 | 32, 32, 4, 1 | 128, 32, 8, 1 |
  | 512 | 64, 16, 8, 1 | 64, 16, 8, 1 |

  Decode-heavy mixed batches with `BLOCK_M // GQA > 16` and fewer than 16 new tokens per request keep the default. With an fp8 query (see below), only configs with `TILE ≥ 32` are used, so head 512 keeps the default.
- **2D decode** (decode batches above the split-KV threshold), as (`TILE`, warps, stages): head 64 (16, 1, 1), 128 (16, 2, 1), 256 (16, 2, 1), 512 (16, 8, 1). With an fp8 query, `TILE` is at least 32.
- **2D/3D switch:** pure decode batches with a 16-bit KV cache use split-KV (3D) up to `64 // num_kv_heads` requests instead of `128 // num_kv_heads`.
- **Split-KV (3D) segments**, head 64/128/256. vLLM always uses 16 segments per request, so the kernel launches requests × KV heads × 16 programs: too few for one request (1 × 2 KV heads × 16 = 32 programs on 32 CUs), and too many tiny ones for larger batches. This PR picks the segment count so that requests × KV heads × segments ≈ 128.
  - 16-bit query: 4 to 128 segments; `TILE` 16, 2 warps, 1 stage.
  - fp8 query: only more segments for small batches (head 256: about 64 programs); head 64 `TILE` 32 / 1 warp, others `TILE` 32 / 4 warps / 2 stages above 16 segments.
  - Sliding windows < 2048 keep 16 segments (head 64: `TILE` 32 / 1 warp, head 128: `TILE` 16 / 1 warp).
  - The scratch the metadata builder allocates is reused as rows × segments. The count depends only on the batch size and the model shape, so it is fixed per CUDA graph.
- **fp8 KV cache:** on gfx1201, `Attention` passes `TRITON_ATTN` an fp8 query; the rules above note where that changes the launch. The 2D/3D switch keeps vLLM's threshold with an fp8 KV cache.

*gfx1100:* applied after the 2D/3D choice, so the 2D/3D threshold is vLLM's.
- **Batches with prefill tokens:** three `max_seqlen_q` bands, as (`BLOCK_M`, `TILE`, warps, stages); "–" keeps the default.

  | head_size | ≤ 64 | 65–4095 | ≥ 4096 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 64 | 16, 32, 2, 1 | 32, 32, 2, 1 | 128, 64, 8, 1 |
  | 128 | – | 64, 32, 4, 1 | 128, 32, 8, 1 |
  | 256 | 32, 32, 8, 1 | 64, 32, 8, 1 | 128, 64, 8, 1 |
  | 512 | 64, 32, 8, 1 | 64, 32, 8, 1 | 64, 32, 8, 1 |

- **2D decode**, as (`TILE`, warps, stages): head 64 (16, 2, 1), 128 (16, 2, 1), 256 (16, 4, 1), 512 (32, 8, 1). `TILE` is raised to 32 with a per-tensor fp8 KV cache.
- **Split-KV (3D) segments:** `next_pow2(T / (requests × KV heads))`, at most 128, with `T` = 512 / 128 / 128 / 64 for head 64 / 128 / 256 / 512. Sliding windows ≥ 512 use 8× as many segments. Sliding-window decode switches to 2D at requests × KV heads ≥ 32 (head 64) / 8 (head 512).
- **fp8 KV cache:** gfx11 has no fp8 matrix instructions, so the query stays bf16 and the configs apply as they are.

**`tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`:**
- New `test_rdna_prefers_triton_attn`. It calls `RocmPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls()` with a mocked arch. Expected selections:
  - gfx1201 and gfx1100 select `TRITON_ATTN`, for the HIP-kernel config (head 128, block 16, bf16, `auto` KV) and for an `fp8` cache;
  - `fp8_e5m2` keeps `ROCM_ATTN`;
  - an explicitly selected `ROCM_ATTN` stays `ROCM_ATTN`;
  - gfx1200 and gfx1101 keep `ROCM_ATTN`.
- Two existing tests that check vLLM's default order now pin `on_gfx1201()` / `on_gfx1100()` to False.

## How it was measured

All measurements call `TRITON_ATTN` (and, for the A/B, `ROCM_ATTN`) as vLLM runs them:
- vLLM's KV-cache allocator, and the backend's own cache writer, metadata builder and `forward()`;
- with an fp8 KV cache, the query is quantized exactly when `Attention` would;
- short-query batches configure speculative decoding, as a server would.

Every output is compared to an fp32 PyTorch reference (causal mask, sliding window, sinks, softcap, ALiBi), within 0.02 + 0.02·|ref|; with an fp8 KV cache, 0.25 + 0.1·|ref|.

Timing:
- each timed call reads its own copy of the KV cache, query and output, with ≥ 512 MB of KV across copies, so data comes from GPU memory and not from L2 / Infinity Cache;
- all copies run in one CUDA graph;
- time per call = graph time / copies.

**Tuning, in order** (each on gfx1201; gfx1100 used the same method):

1. **2D launch configs**, against `TRITON_ATTN`'s default launch.
   - Shapes: head 64/128/256 × GQA 1–16 × KV heads per GPU 1–8 × block 16/528 (138 shapes), plus head 512 (Gemma 4's global layers, 5 shapes).
   - Batches: 214 per shape (decode, prefill, chunked prefill, mixed).
   - Configs: `BLOCK_M` × `TILE` × warps × stages. A pilot timed every config on 2 shapes; a greedy cover kept the fewest configs within 2% of the best on every pilot batch.
   - Rule: per head size and region, the simplest rule (one config per band) close to the per-shape best, and ≥ 0.97× the default on almost every batch.
   - 29,532 measurements, 0 wrong outputs. Over the default launch on prefill-containing batches: 2.32× (head 64), 2.12× (128), 1.82× (256), 3.41× (512).
2. **2D/3D switch:** 3,888 decode and short-query batches, each run forced-2D and forced-3D. Under full CUDA graphs the choice is frozen per captured batch size, so the rule can only depend on batch size. Decode: half of vLLM's threshold; short queries: vLLM's.
3. **Split-KV segments:** 1,534 + 880 batches; segments 4–128 × 6 launch configs; head 64–512, GQA 3–16, KV heads 1–8, sliding windows, fp8. The best count follows requests × KV heads (about 128 programs), in both directions.
4. **Against `ROCM_ATTN`, through the backend:**
   - every HIP-kernel layout (4,245 batches);
   - a head-64 decode sweep: 16 launch variants × 256 batches (found the head-64 2D decode config: 1 warp);
   - a 1-warp sweep over every remaining regression cluster: 12 variants × 538 batches (chose 2 warps for split-KV; 1 warp lost everywhere except head-64 2D decode and short sliding windows).

**Final A/B: upstream vs this PR** (the results below).
- Two checkouts of the same vLLM build: upstream (`dde9aca41c`, this PR's base) and this PR.
- For every config and batch, each tree runs the backend it selects by default. Speedup = upstream time / PR time (> 1: this PR is faster).
- 14,608 batches; KV caches above 4 GB are skipped.

| region | what |
|---|---|
| `hip` | every layout where `ROCM_ATTN` uses its HIP decode kernel: head 128, block 16, bf16/fp16, GQA 3/4/5/6/8/10/12/16 × KV heads 1/2/4/8, plus softcap. Decode 1–64 requests × 1k–128k |
| `nonhip` | plain attention elsewhere: head 64/96/128/192/256/512 × GQA 1–16 × block 16/528, bf16/fp16 |
| `variants`, `fp16_variants` | sliding window 2048, sinks, sliding window 128 + sinks (gpt-oss), softcap, ALiBi; bf16 and fp16 |
| `fp8` | fp8 KV cache, plain and sliding window, head 64–512, block 16/528 |
| `prefill_mixed`, `qlen`, `spec` | prefill (128–8192 tokens, chunks on 16k–128k), mixed batches, query lengths 9–128, spec-decode verification (2–8 tokens) |
| `lowfill_3d`, `highconc` | 1–16 requests at every head size and block size (incl. 64k); 7–256 requests around the 2D/3D switch |
| `swa_decode`, `gptoss`, `blocksizes` | sliding windows 256–4096 (incl. Muse Glimmer); gpt-oss shapes; block 32/64 |

Batch families:

| family | batches |
|---|---|
| decode | 1–256 requests × 1k–128k context |
| spec decode | 2–8 new tokens per request |
| prefill | fresh prompts and chunks on cached context |
| mixed | 1–4 prefill chunks + 4–63 decodes |

Causes, by cluster:
- **softcap:** the cost of the tanh softcap in the Triton kernel. Only Gemma 2 uses an attention softcap in vLLM (head 256, and head 128 at GQA 2), where this PR is faster; the head-128 GQA 3–16 and head-64 softcap shapes don't occur in supported models;
- **split-KV decode at 1k–4k context:** split / merge overhead when each segment covers few tokens;
- **head-128 2D decode at GQA 1–2, 8–64 requests,** and **head-256 2D decode at 32–64 requests:** `ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton decode kernel is a few percent faster there;
- **fp8 KV, head 64, one fresh 1k–4k prompt:** upstream's prefill reads the new tokens unquantized, while `TRITON_ATTN` reads them back from the fp8 cache.

- **split-KV decode at 16–128 requests, head 64 / 128** (plain, ALiBi, softcap): these batches keep vLLM's default split-KV launch (16 segments; the gfx1100 segment rule only adds segments at low fill). `ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton 2D decode kernel is faster there; the gap is the backend swap, not a launch config;
- **head-64 2D decode at 128–256 requests:** same, `ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton 2D decode kernel is faster at very high concurrency;
- **fp8 KV, head 64, one fresh 1k–9k prompt:** upstream's prefill reads the new tokens unquantized, while `TRITON_ATTN` reads them back from the fp8 cache (as on gfx1201);
- **sliding-window decode, head 512 / 64, fp8 KV, 1–8k context:** the switch to 2D for sliding-window decode; it is 2.25× faster with a 16-bit KV cache, but about neutral with fp8 (worst 0.30× at 1k);
- **many 48–128-token chunks on 32k context:** `ROCM_ATTN`'s prefix-prefill kernel is faster for that shape.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel][DSv4.1] Swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention for small TP2/TP4 steps
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

  Makes DeepSeek-V4.1's per-layer decode attention step **1.4-2.15x faster** for decode steps of up to 16 tokens at TP2 / TP4, by adding a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention kernel to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer (#56935) on SM10x. Steps of up to 16
  tokens with 16 or 32 live heads per rank (TP4 / TP2 of the 64-head model) now take it instead of the mega kernel, which pads the heads to 64.
  Part of #57448; it reads the interleaved V4.1 KV records from #61371. Related work that this PR does not duplicate (see Details): #59418, #61615, #57711, #61868.

  ## Claims

  - **1.4-2.15x faster decode attention for 1-16 tokens:** 1.8-2.15x with 16 live heads (TP4) and 1.4-1.8x with 32 (TP2), for both NVFP4 and fp8 compressed records (per-layer Q pad + KV insert + attention, table below; the lower ends are B300). End to end at TP2 this is 4.5-7.6% lower median TPOT at concurrency 1-16 (see the A/B comment). The mega kernel's FP8 decode maps
  query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads; swap-AB puts the KV slots on M and only the live heads on N.
  - **Accuracy:** the output's error against an fp64 reference is at most 1.1x the mega kernel's, and the output is within 2% of the mega kernel's, over 64 test cases.
  - **Automatic and contained.** There is no new flag, environment variable or config option. Every other decode step, layer and TP size keeps the mega kernel; prefill and other platforms are unchanged. The new kernel is CUDA-graph safe and deterministic,
  and adds no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Performance.** This PR adds a swap-AB arm to the existing `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`. Each arm's per-step ops (Q pad + KV insert + attention) are timed as a CUDA graph replay, the same harness that produced the mega vs split-KV
  table in `flash_mla_mega_attn.py`.

  ```bash
  for heads in 16 32; do
    for rec in 288 528; do
      .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py \
          --local-heads $heads --extra-bytes $rec --decode-s-q 1 2 4 8 16 32 64
    done
  done
  ```

  Speedup = mega step time / swap-AB step time (median of two runs, which differ by at most 9% per cell):

  | Live heads | Compressed record | 1 token | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 16 (TP4) | NVFP4 (288 B) | **2.15x** | **2.00x** | **2.06x** | **1.94x** | **2.04x** | 1.25x | 0.94x |
  | 16 (TP4) | fp8 (528 B) | **2.13x** | **1.96x** | **2.02x** | **1.90x** | **1.99x** | 1.22x | 0.91x |
  | 32 (TP2) | fp8 (528 B) | **1.76x** | **1.66x** | **1.71x** | **1.62x** | **1.71x** | 0.98x | 0.73x |

  At 32 tokens swap-AB still wins with 16 heads (1.22-1.25x) but only breaks even with 32 (0.98-1.02x), and at 64 it loses with both, so `_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS = 16` is the largest step size where it wins for both head counts. On B300 (nightly 76c6f3f2) the same harness gives 1.83-2.0x with 16 heads and 1.41-1.64x with 32 heads at 1-16 tokens, for both record formats. As in the existing harness,
  every replay reuses the same buffers, so the KV reads hit a warm L2 for both kernels; timed alone with the L2 flushed before every call, the attention kernel is 1.6-2.3x faster than the mega kernel over 48 shapes with 1-16 tokens (geomean 1.94x).

  **Correctness: unit tests.** The kernel tests skip unless the GPU is SM10x and the CuTe DSL is built with CUDA 13.2+.

  ```bash
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_swapab_decode.py
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode"
  ```

  | Test (cases) | Checks | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `test_matches_reference` (64) | 16/32 heads x 1/2/5/16 tokens x NVFP4/fp8 compressed records x 64/128-slot pages x partial/full lengths. Output is finite; Frobenius and max-abs error vs an fp64 reference are <= 1.1x the mega kernel's; within 2% of the
  mega output | 64 passed |
  | `test_untouched_padding` (2) | Padding heads' output groups keep their bytes | 2 passed |
  | `test_cuda_graph_and_determinism` (12) | Repeated eager calls and a CUDA graph replay agree bit for bit, also after the inputs change in place | 12 passed |
  | `test_dispatch_rule` (9, CPU) | Which kernel each dispatch condition selects | 9 passed |
  | `test_warmup_key_matches_launch` (4, CPU) | The key the layer registers at construction is the key a decode step launches, on a compressed cache shaped as the model runner binds it | 4 passed |
  | `test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode` (3, existing) | The V4.1 cache writers and FlashMLA agree on the interleaved records the kernel reads | 3 passed |

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention is the default DeepSeek V4.1 decode path on SM10x. Its FP8 decode kernel takes 64 or 128 query heads, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads. The mega vs split-KV note in
  `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` already records that this padded-head cost dominates small decode steps. Small steps are what low-concurrency decode and spec-decode verify and draft steps run.

  **Why a separate kernel, not a FlashMLA change.** FlashMLA's decode maps query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64. Serving 16 or 32 heads without padding needs the opposite mapping, with KV slots on M and heads on N. That is a
  different kernel, not a smaller tile. In FlashMLA it would be CUDA C++ shipped through a vllm-project/FlashMLA release and a vLLM bump, as #61371 was. The CuTe DSL kernel instead compiles from Python at JIT warmup, needs no build change, and lives next
  to its only caller in the DSv4.1 model package. It is adapted from SGLang's swap-AB DSv4 decode attention (Apache-2.0, attribution in the file header).

  <details>
  <summary>Kernel design</summary>

  - **MMA shape.** `SwapABDecodeKernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/swapab_decode_attn.py`) puts the KV slots on the tcgen05 MMA's M side (128 rows) and the live heads on N (16 or 32).
  - **One CTA per (token, KV tile).** Tiles are 64 slots of the SWA list or 128 slots of the compressed list. Each CTA:
    - gathers its slots' V4.1 records in place (fp8 528 B, NVFP4 288 B, each token's scales after its data);
    - dequantizes them exactly to bf16 in SMEM;
    - RoPEs Q in fp32 from the mega kernel's chunk-interleaved, head-padded layout;
    - computes S = KV Q^T and O = KV^T P, with P split into bf16 hi and lo parts.
  - **One cluster per token.** A token's tiles form one thread-block cluster: 6 CTAs for V4.1-Flash's 128-slot window plus 512 compressed slots. The cluster merges the partials and the attention sink over DSMEM in a fixed peer order. It then applies the
  inverse RoPE and writes MXFP8 with the mega kernel's rounding rule into the o-fused buffers `wo_a` reads, for the live heads' groups only.
  - **One launch.** The kernel uses PDL and has no workspace, second kernel, allocation or host sync.
  - **JIT warmup.** The compile key is (live heads, slot-list widths, compressed record size, SWA and compressed page sizes); the token count is the grid's y dimension. Every field is fixed when the layer is built: the backend has one kernel block size (128), so a compressed page always holds
  `128 // compress_ratio` slots, whatever the KV cache manager's block size. The layer registers the key in `__init__`, next to its other JIT warmups, and `kernel_warmup` compiles it before CUDA graph capture. V4.1-Flash needs two keys, one per compressed page size.

  </details>

  **Dispatch.** `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention._forward_decode_mega` takes the swap-AB kernel only when all of these hold:
  - the GPU is SM10x;
  - the layer has a compressed cache;
  - the layer has 16 or 32 live heads;
  - a token's tiles fit one portable cluster: `ceil(window / 64) + ceil(index_topk / 128) <= 8`;
  - the CuTe DSL imports and was built with CUDA 13.2+, which the direct fp8 / fp4 to bf16x2 conversions need (PTX ISA 9.2);
  - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off;
  - the step has at most 16 decode tokens (`_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS`). Under CUDA graphs this is the padded count, so each captured graph holds exactly one of the two kernels;
  - the step's SWA list is exactly the window. DSpark's non-causal draft steps widen it, so they keep the mega kernel.

  The first six conditions are fixed when the layer is built. The last two are host-side shape checks on each step. If any condition fails, the step runs the mega kernel exactly as before.
  **Complexity.** The change adds about 1,260 lines of kernel code (about 400 of them are 23 small inline-PTX wrappers) and about 100 lines in the layer. Nothing changes in the model runner, the scheduler, FlashMLA or shared attention code. At runtime the
  kernel module is imported only by SM10x layers with a compressed cache, 16 or 32 heads and an importable CuTe DSL. Most of the maintenance cost is the inline PTX and the SMEM / TMEM layout math. Both are documented next to the code, and the tests pin
  them to an fp64 reference and to the mega kernel.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - **Cost grows with tokens.** The kernel runs one cluster of up to 8 CTAs per token, and its 150+ KiB of SMEM means one CTA per SM. Hence the 16-token cutoff, which is the same for TP2 / TP4 and both record formats: in the table above swap-AB is at
  least 1.6x faster at every step size up to 16 tokens (at least 1.4x on B300).
  - **Not bit-identical.** The fp32 sums are ordered differently from the mega kernel's, so the output depends on which kernel the step size selects. Batch-invariant runs therefore keep the mega kernel at every size.
  - **Unused Q padding.** The fused KV insert still zero-pads Q to 64 heads, which swap-AB does not read. This keeps one Q contract for both kernels.
  - **Toolchain.** The kernel needs a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+. With an older build the layer keeps the mega kernel and the kernel tests skip.
  - **Startup.** V4.1-Flash adds two JIT compiles per worker, at warmup.

  **Compatibility.**
  - **Scope.** Only `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention` changes. The FlashMLA sparse layer, FlashInfer sparse MLA, and the SM90, SM120 and ROCm paths are untouched. TP1 (64 heads) and TP8 (8 heads) keep the mega kernel.
  - **Model runners.** Both V1 and V2 build the model under the JIT warmup registry, so both register the key.
  - **CUDA graphs, batch invariance, spec decode.** See Dispatch above.
  - **Unchanged.** Prefill, the KV cache layout and checkpoints.

  **CI.** The new tests run in the optional (nightly) 4xB200 step, renamed "(4xB200) DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA Kernels" (`models_basic.yaml`, key `dsv41-nvidia-kernels-4xb200`), next to the specialized-decode tests. The kernel tests need SM10x, the FlashMLA mega ops and a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+, and skip otherwise; with vLLM's pinned `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0` they run. The optional "(B200)
  LM Eval Spec Decode" step runs the V4.1-Flash NVFP4 DSpark TP4 GSM8K config. It runs at full concurrency, where few steps are small enough for swap-AB.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched GitHub (open PRs plus PRs since 2026-08-15) for "swap-AB", "swapab", "small-head decode", "heads padded 64 decode", "mega attention DSv4.1" and "V4.1 decode attention". No PR adds an SM10x small-head decode
  kernel for the mega-attention path. Related work:
  - **#59418** (open, small-head sparse decode on SM90) is a Triton kernel for Hopper. It targets 8 or 16 heads in the plain FlashMLA sparse layer, which reads the 584 B `fp8_ds_mla` records used off SM10x. This PR targets SM10x tcgen05 and 16 or 32 heads
  in the mega-attention layer, which reads the V4.1 records and fuses the inverse RoPE and MXFP8 output.
  - **#61615** (open) is small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM90. This PR changes decode only, on SM10x.
  - **#57711** (closed by its author on 2026-09-25) was an opt-in split-KV mode inside the mega decode kernel, behind the `VLLM_DSV41_MEGA_SPLITKV` env flags and blocked on vllm-project/FlashMLA#25. That kernel still pads the heads to 64. This PR leaves
  FlashMLA alone, removes the padded-head work and adds no flags.
  - **#61868** (open) is an opt-in GB300 TP4 DSpark executor whose sparse-MLA decode uses FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4`. That is a separate opt-in path; this PR changes the default mega-attention path.

  **AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). It drafted the port of the kernel onto main, the tests, the benchmark arm, the `/pr-checklist` pass and this description. The submitter reviewed every changed
  line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Share one RoPE cache across Muse Spark NVIDIA layers
commits.pr_body:
_Requested by **Simon**_



## Overview

The NVIDIA Muse Spark model builds a private fp32 RoPE table in each of its 46 RoPE attention layers. The tables are identical and cost 11.5 GiB per GPU. This PR shares one table, as #62757 did for the ROCm path.

Fixes #65205

## Claims

- Model loading drops from 81.0 to 69.75 GiB per GPU on 8x B200, TP8, `Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`.
- The KV cache grows from 9,248,688 to 10,589,618 tokens (+14.5 %).
- Output does not change: greedy output is bit-identical, and GSM8K-100 is 96/100 on stock and 95/100 with this PR, which is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

New unit test `tests/models/test_muse_spark_nvidia_shared_rope.py`, CPU only, with the heavy submodules stubbed. It mirrors `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` from #62757.

- Two target layers must hold the same fp32 `RotaryEmbedding`.
- It uses its own empty `_ROPE_DICT`, so the CPU tables it builds do not leak into later GPU tests (the failure #65138 and #65140 fixed for the ROCm twin).

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest -v tests/models/test_muse_spark_nvidia_shared_rope.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py
```

On this branch: 16 passed. Without the model change, the new test fails (two different objects). The test is added to the "Basic Models (Other)" step next to its ROCm twin.

End to end on 8x B200, TP8, `unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`, default `max_model_len` (1,048,576), with prefix caching. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-76c6f3f2a95f6049657db1e513133b824a5c8175` (digest `sha256:7a933b7c…`), the newest nightly; no nightly at this base exists yet. `nvidia/model.py` is byte-identical on 76c6f3f2a and this PR's base, so the PR arm loaded this branch's `nvidia/model.py` on that image. Each arm ran on a fresh server start, and each start logged the sha256 of the file that was loaded.

| Check | Stock | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model loading per GPU | 81.0 GiB | 69.75 GiB |
| Available KV cache memory, TP0 | 90.01 GiB | 101.26 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 9,248,688 tokens | 10,589,618 tokens (+14.5 %) |
| Greedy, 8 prompts × 256 tokens, one at a time | reference | 8/8 bit-identical |
| GSM8K-100, temperature 0, 32 concurrent | 96/100 | 95/100 |

The saving is 11.25 GiB, which is 45 × 256 MiB: one table remains. The GSM8K gap is batch-order noise: the four questions only stock got right hit the 6,000-token cap in a reasoning loop on this PR's arm. Stock shows the same loops (it hit the cap twice). An earlier pair of runs on the same patch scored 97/100 on both arms.

On the same pod, an earlier version of the new test (the sharing check plus a bit-equality check against a private table) and the ROCm twin passed against this PR's `nvidia/model.py`. Against the stock file, the sharing check failed. The GPU runs used a version of `nvidia/model.py` that differs from this PR only in two code comments.

Sanity pass on fresh starts of the same setup. Without speculative decoding, 100 varied prompts (chat, code, math, 8k-token summaries, tool calls, multilingual, JSON, multi-turn) gave token-identical output on stock and this PR, greedy and 30 seeded samples at temperature 0.7. With the DSpark draft from the recipe (`Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark`, 7 speculative tokens), whose RoPE table this PR leaves private, the acceptance rate was 0.2679 on stock and 0.2680 with this PR (mean acceptance length 2.875 and 2.876). The KV cache grew from 5,043,740 to 6,359,813 tokens. Greedy output was 93/100 identical; a second stock start was 92/100 identical to the first, with differences only on the 8k-token prompts in both cases. On this base, DSpark fails to load on stock, because `MuseSparkDSparkModel` never sets `_context_kv_proj` (read in `qwen3_dflash.py` `load_weights`). Both spec arms set it to `None` for the test; that is a separate bug.

Not measured: performance. No kernel changes, and the kernels read the same table values.

## Details

Root cause, in `vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/model.py`:

- Each target `MuseSpark1xAttention` with RoPE constructs its own `RotaryEmbedding` with an fp32 `cos_sin_cache` of `[max_position, 64]`.
- `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer` passes `max(config.max_position_embeddings, max_model_len)`, so the table has at least 1,048,576 rows whatever `--max-model-len` is.
- 46 of the 62 layers use RoPE, all with theta 500000. 46 × 1,048,576 × 64 × 4 B = 11.5 GiB.

Change:

- Target layers take their table from `get_rope(..., dtype=torch.float, rope_parameters={"rope_theta": theta, "rope_type": "default"})`. `get_rope` caches one instance per key, so all 46 layers share one table.
- `MuseSpark1xDecoderLayer` sizes the target table by `max_model_len`, since target positions never reach it. With a smaller `--max-model-len` the table shrinks too (64 MiB at 262,144); that case was not run end to end.
- The DSpark draft keeps its private table, dtype and size.

Numerics: each row of the table is computed the same way whatever the table length, and sharing does not change any value. On the unfused path, `_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype` now converts one shared table instead of 46 identical ones, with the same result.

Related: #63078 (open) keeps these tables fp32 at the unfused call sites. It touches different lines of `nvidia/model.py` and applies cleanly on top of this branch. #65170 (open, ROCm) moves the shared table to CUDA before the ROCm monokernel reads it; the NVIDIA path has no monokernel, and the fused kernel worked with the shared table in the runs above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Keep 32-bit buffer addressing for per-token-head KV and AITER cross-attention fallback
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

<!-- Summarize the change in 1-2 lines. Link relevant issues and PRs. -->

Follow-up to #60084. On ROCm, two more paths now give their KV-cache views a Triton `ptr_range()`, so Triton's AMD backend keeps 32-bit buffer addressing for them:
- the per-token-head quantized KV cache (`int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`) in `TRITON_ATTN`;
- the non-causal fallback of `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, which runs vLLM's `kernel_unified_attention` for encoder-decoder cross-attention.

Updated to current `main`, which now includes the extensible KV cache (#56492). How the two interact is described under Details.

## Claims

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

- Throughput on Radeon Pro W7900 (gfx1100), current `main`, default settings:
  - **+56%** for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `TRITON_ATTN` with an `int8_per_token_head` KV cache: 1.93 → 3.02 req/s.
  - **+60%** for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with an `fp8_per_token_head` KV cache: 2.01 → 3.22 req/s.
- When the extensible KV cache is off (V1 model runner, explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, or no VMM support):
  - **+49%** for gpt-oss-20b with an `int8_per_token_head` KV cache: 2.46 → 3.66 req/s.
  - **+1%** for Whisper-large-v3 on `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`: 6.88 → 6.95 req/s.
- No regressions: AITER's own causal kernel is not touched, and the other workloads measured are unchanged.
- No accuracy change: Whisper transcripts are token-identical, and GSM8K with per-token-head KV caches (Qwen2.5-7B, gpt-oss-20b) is within run-to-run noise.
- 6 lines in two files; no new configuration.

## Validation

<!-- Show evidence that the claims are met by this change, and steps to reproduce validations. -->

W7900 (gfx1100), ROCm 10.2, PyTorch 2.14, Triton 3.8.0. Base = this PR's parent, using the same build (the change is Python-only). Base and PR runs alternated on the same GPU. Each variant started from an empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, warmed by an untimed first run.

**Current `main` (c7a7607519), extensible KV cache on by default**

| `vllm bench throughput`, random 1024 / 256, 500 prompts unless noted | base (3 runs) | this PR (3 runs) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, bf16, `TRITON_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head` | 1.93 / 1.93 / 1.93 | 3.02 / 3.02 / 3.02 | **+56%** |
| Same, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_per_token_head` | 2.01 / 2.01 / 2.01 | 3.21 / 3.22 / 3.22 | **+60%** |
| gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4 MoE, sinks, sliding window), `TRITON_ATTN`, `int8_per_token_head` | 2.48 / 2.49 / 2.48 | 2.48 / 2.48 / 2.48 | ±0 (see Details) |
| Whisper-large-v3, fp16, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, LibriSpeech, 100 prompts × 200 tokens | 7.03 / 7.02 / 7.02 | 7.02 / 7.02 / 7.02 | ±0 (see Details) |

**Current `main`, `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`**

| `vllm bench throughput` | base (2 runs) | this PR (2 runs) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, `TRITON_ATTN`, `int8_per_token_head` | 2.46 / 2.46 | 3.66 / 3.66 | **+49%** |
| Whisper-large-v3, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | 6.88 / 6.87 | 6.95 / 6.94 | **+1%** |

<details>
<summary>Earlier measurements on the parent before #56492 (5ea8301982), 3 runs per side</summary>

| `vllm bench throughput` | base | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `int8_per_token_head` | 1.99 / 1.99 / 1.99 | 3.04 / 3.04 / 3.04 | +53% |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `fp8_per_token_head` | 2.10 / 2.10 / 2.10 | 3.19 / 3.20 / 3.19 | +52% |
| gpt-oss-20b, `int8_per_token_head` | 2.45 / 2.45 / 2.45 | 3.67 / 3.67 / 3.67 | +50% |
| gpt-oss-20b, `fp8_per_token_head` | 2.55 / 2.55 / 2.55 | 3.71 / 3.71 / 3.71 | +45% |
| Whisper-large-v3, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | 6.83 / 6.83 / 6.84 | 6.91 / 6.91 / 6.93 | +1.2% |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` (decoder-only, AITER's causal kernel) | 3.87 / 3.87 / 3.87 | 3.87 / 3.87 / 3.87 | ±0 |
</details>

| Accuracy | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Whisper, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, 32 LibriSpeech clips, greedy (current `main`) | — | 32 / 32 token-identical |
| GSM8K, Qwen2.5-7B, `int8_per_token_head`, 5-shot, strict / flexible (current `main`) | 78.01 / 81.50 | 79.00 / 82.34 |
| GSM8K, Qwen2.5-7B, `int8_per_token_head`, 5-shot, strict-match, 3 runs (parent before #56492) | 79.23 / 79.23 / 77.86 (mean 78.77) | 78.17 / 78.62 / 79.00 (mean 78.60) |
| GSM8K, gpt-oss-20b, `int8_per_token_head`, chat template, 0-shot, 2048 tokens, flexible-extract, 3 runs (parent before #56492) | 85.75 / 85.37 / 86.20 (mean 85.77) | 86.28 / 86.20 / 86.05 (mean 86.18) |
| Same, `fp8_per_token_head` | 85.52 / 85.29 / 86.28 (mean 85.70) | 85.67 / 85.60 / 86.28 (mean 85.85) |

GSM8K stderr is ±1.1 for Qwen and ±1.0 for gpt-oss. Greedy Qwen outputs can't be compared token for token: with `TRITON_ATTN` (compile + CUDA graphs), `main` itself is not run-to-run deterministic on this GPU (base-vs-base agreed on 37–43 of 128 prompts; 58 of 128 for BF16).

<details>
<summary>Code generation, profile and lint</summary>

- **Code generation** (Triton cache of each run, current `main`):
  - Per-token-head (Qwen2.5-7B): `key_cache_ptr`, `value_cache_ptr`, `k_scale_cache_ptr` and `v_scale_cache_ptr` carry `tt.pointer_range = 32` in `kernel_unified_attention` and `_reshape_cache_per_token_head`. FP8 split-KV decode: 252 → 191 VGPRs. INT8: 242 → 239 VGPRs; the gain there comes from 32-bit address arithmetic on the four pointers.
  - gpt-oss-20b with the extensible KV cache off: split-KV decode variants 255/256 → 156/167 VGPRs (INT8).
  - AITER fallback: `kernel_unified_attention` K/V gain `tt.pointer_range = 32`, 255 → 205 VGPRs.
- **Why AITER's causal kernel is excluded** (measured before #56492):
  - Hinting it as well gives its K/V `tt.pointer_range = 32` without lowering its VGPRs (232–240; 256 for `_3d`).
  - A rocprofv3 trace shows its `_2d` decode variant 5.9% slower per call (715.8 → 758.2 µs); Qwen on `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` lost 0.8%.
- **Host overhead:** `set_triton_ptr_range` costs ~1 µs per call. A `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` run on both changed paths passes.
- **Lint:** `pre-commit run` (ruff, mypy, typos, …) passes on the changed files.
- **No new tests:** the change only affects code generation, and CI has no RDNA runners.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE=TRUE
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --attention-config.backend TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 500 --seed 0
# gpt-oss-20b: same with --model openai/gpt-oss-20b, plus --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache for the second table
vllm bench throughput --model openai/whisper-large-v3 --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --dtype float16 --max-model-len 448 \
  --attention-config.backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openslr/librispeech_asr --hf-subset clean --hf-split validation \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":1}' --num-prompts 100 --backend vllm --output-len 200
# GSM8K: lm_eval.simple_evaluate(model=VLLM(pretrained="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", dtype="bfloat16",
#   max_model_len=4096, attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}, kv_cache_dtype="int8_per_token_head"),
#   tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5)
# gpt-oss-20b: pretrained="openai/gpt-oss-20b", num_fewshot=0, apply_chat_template=True,
#   gen_kwargs="max_gen_toks=2048,temperature=0"; score = flexible-extract
```
</details>

## Details

<!-- Explain motivation, design decisions, root cause, tradeoffs, and limitations concisely. Link or collapse lengthy supporting material. -->

**Root cause.**
- #60084 fixed the 32-bit addressing loss caused by #51718's single KV-cache allocation, but only for the K/V views built in `TritonAttentionImpl.forward` and `do_kv_cache_update`.
- The per-token-head path builds its views in `_pth_key_value_caches()`. Its per-(token, head) scale caches are strided float32 views of the same storage.
- The AITER backend calls `kernel_unified_attention` directly for non-causal attention.
- In all these cases Triton's `is_within_2gb` saw the whole allocation and chose 64-bit addressing.

**Change.**
- `TritonAttentionImpl`, on ROCm (existing `_set_kv_ptr_range` flag):
  - `_ensure_scale_caches()` sets the bound once on the two scale caches when it creates them;
  - `_pth_key_value_caches()` sets it on the K/V views on every call.
- `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionImpl.forward` sets it on the K/V views right before the non-causal fallback call.
- All reuse `set_triton_ptr_range` from #60084; the bound is the distance from each view's `data_ptr()` to the end of the layer's region.

**Interaction with the extensible KV cache (#56492).**
- Until warmup ends, each layer's view spans the layer's whole *reservation*; CUDA graphs are captured in this phase. After `extend_kv_cache`, `committed_views()` rebinds each layer to storage of exactly its committed blocks.
- Eager launches after the extend therefore get 32-bit addressing without any hint (Whisper above: base = PR). The fallback hint still matters when the extensible cache is off.
- Kernels captured in CUDA graphs keep the binary compiled during warmup. When a layer's reservation is ≤ 2 GiB (Qwen2.5-7B), this PR gives them 32-bit addressing. When it exceeds 2 GiB, nothing can: gpt-oss-20b INT8 here reserves 126,664 blocks × 17,408 B = 2.05 GiB per layer, while the committed size is 1.64 GiB. Traced inside the engine, the hint reports 2.054 GiB during capture and 1.641 GiB afterwards, and Triton correctly refuses the first.
- This also affects #60084, is independent of this PR, and is better handled separately.

**Safety.**
- The scale and K/V offsets the kernels compute are non-negative and stay within the layer: block-table index × block stride + slot/head/channel offsets.
- Triton still checks the bound against 2 GiB at every launch. `set_triton_ptr_range` reads only shapes, strides and `data_ptr()`; it never touches uncommitted memory.
- The INT4 per-token-head kernel and AITER's causal kernel are unchanged.

**Limitations.**
- Measured on RDNA3 only.
- Not covered:
  - `TRITON_MLA` / AITER MLA `decode_attention_fwd`, which reviewers of #60084 measured a CDNA gain on; left for a separate PR;
  - `TritonAttentionDiffKVImpl` and the gfx1250 shuffled-KV Triton cache write.

**Duplicates.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `ptr_range`, `set_triton_ptr_range`, per-token-head + `ptr_range`, and AITER cross-attention; only #60084 overlaps.

commits.pr_body: Enable encoder CUDA Graphs for Mistral multimodal models using the Pixtral vision encoder, covering both `PixtralForConditionalGeneration` and `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` The implementation packs variable-resolution image patches into fixed-capacity graph buffers and precomputes attention metadata, rotary embeddings, and patch-merger indices. Unsupported attention configurations fall back to eager execution. It also keeps `max_seqlen` on CPU because attention backends call `.item()` on it during capture. ## Relation to existing work PR #54214 independently implements the native Pixtral path and overlaps part of this change. This implementation additionally covers `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` path, validates actual serving on Mistral Large 3 NVFP4 with TP=4, supports the relevant FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, and ROCm AITER metadata paths, and includes reproducible profiling and performance scripts. commits.pr_title: [Perf][Startup] Keep openai out of import vllm.config via lazy ToolServer import
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Every vLLM process imports `vllm.config`, and `vllm.config.reasoning` → `vllm.reasoning` → `abs_reasoning_parsers` imports `vllm.entrypoints.mcp.tool_server` at module level, which pulls in `openai` and `openai_harmony`. `ToolServer` is only used in a type annotation there, so this PR moves the import under `TYPE_CHECKING`. This is the "`vllm.config.reasoning` → `entrypoints.mcp` → `openai.types`" item in #59433, and the PR extends `tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py` as the issue proposes.

## Claims

- `import vllm.config` no longer imports `openai` / `openai_harmony` (524 modules before, 0 after on CPU; checked on CUDA as well).
- `vllm.config.reasoning` cumulative import time drops from ~310-440 ms to ~6-9 ms (`python -X importtime -c "import vllm.config"`, CPU, 3 runs).
- `tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py` now fails if `import vllm.config` imports `openai` again (see the CI note below).

## Validation

```bash
python3 tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py
pytest tests/reasoning
```

```text
# main
vllm/config/__init__.py:43 from vllm.config.reasoning import ReasoningConfig
vllm/config/reasoning.py:8 from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParserManager
vllm/reasoning/__init__.py:4 from vllm.reasoning.abs_reasoning_parsers import ...
vllm/reasoning/abs_reasoning_parsers.py:10 from vllm.entrypoints.mcp.tool_server import ToolServer
vllm/entrypoints/mcp/tool_server.py:9 from vllm.entrypoints.mcp.tool import ...
vllm/entrypoints/mcp/tool.py:8 from openai.types.responses ...
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai.types'; 'openai' is not a package
exit 1

# this PR
exit 0
```

Same result on CPU (macOS, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`) and on 1x NVIDIA B300 with vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2a` (both touched files are identical to this branch's base). After `import vllm.config`, `"openai" in sys.modules` is `True` on main and `False` with this PR on both.

| `-X importtime`, CPU, ms (3 runs) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm.config.reasoning` cumulative | 439 / 408 / 310 | 5.6 / 6.5 / 9.2 |
| `import vllm.config` total | 4987 / 4705 / 4395 | 4364 / 4071 / 3864 |

`pytest tests/reasoning` on CPU: 485 passed on main and with this PR. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pre-commit run --files` pass on the changed files.

## Details

- `abs_reasoning_parsers.py` has no `from __future__ import annotations`, so the one annotation that uses `ToolServer` (`prepare_structured_tag`) is quoted. Nothing in the file uses `ToolServer` at runtime.
- `lazy_imports.py` blocks `openai` the same way it blocks `cv2`, and adds `import vllm.config`, since `import vllm` alone does not import the config package.
- The API server still imports `openai` through the OpenAI entrypoints; this only keeps it out of the shared config import that EngineCore and workers also pay for.
- CI: `lazy_imports.py` currently runs only in the `(CPU) Params, Env, Tokenizers, Parser` job, which is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` (disabled by #63609). #64414 restores it. I left the Buildkite config alone to keep this PR small.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `abs_reasoning_parsers.py` or blocks `openai` in `lazy_imports.py`. #57310 also adds lines after `import vllm  # noqa` in `lazy_imports.py`, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to draft the change, the test and this description. I reviewed the changes, the measurements and the test results before submitting.

[Bugfix][Benchmark] Preserve inactive expert IDs in synthetic forward routing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preserve inactive `-1` expert IDs in `vllm bench forward`'s Zipf and balanced routing hook. Previously, substituting the synthetic fixture could reactivate masked expert slots.

## Claims

- Inactive slots remain `-1`; active slots receive the same synthetic IDs and routing weights remain unchanged.
- The fixture is not mutated, so subsequent replays can activate previously inactive slots.

## Validation

The focused regression failed all four parameters without the fix and passed with it (positional/keyword IDs, int32/int64). The existing Zipf selection test also passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  -k 'synthetic_expert_ids_preserve_inactive_slots or zipf_expert_selection' -q
```

On GB200, the real Muse router/bias test and both tiny Muse CLI configurations passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  -k 'muse_synthetic_routing or balanced_routing_restores_expert_bias' -v
```

Balanced and Zipf each produced finite, deterministic prefill/decode output with exact graph/eager equality. The CLI uses the gate-logits path without capture-bucket padding; the focused hook regression establishes sentinel preservation. This does not claim end-to-end padded EP performance validation.

File-scoped pre-commit checks passed. GPU validation used `78fc2bbed0`; the rebased routing, test and documentation files are byte-identical. The rebase only reconciled the CI selector with upstream additions. [Validation details](https://github.com/Inferact/vllm-perf-data/blob/main/patches/forward-zipf-padding.md).

## Details

The generic expert-input hook replaced the entire ID tensor without preserving its inactive sentinel. A tensor selection now retains existing `-1` entries. This adds comparison/selection work inside the timed generic hook, without host synchronization. The gate-logits hook and production serving are unchanged. Docs clarify exact-shape benchmark graphs versus serving capture-bucket padding.

Duplicate checks found no competing fix. #64167 introduced the Zipf default and is merged; #57100 concerns the separate MoE kernel benchmark, #65085 concerns forward batch budgets, and #52532 concerns Marlin token ordering.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation, validation, and PR preparation.

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Support ModelOpt CUTLASS FP8 weight-cache restarts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Enable serialized ModelOpt per-tensor and per-channel FP8 linear weights to be reused by the weight-cache daemon with CUTLASS. Related to #56049; depends on #63672 for restoring CUTLASS's logical output width. Incremental review: https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/35711168b0135573234bbaa4bd8f9e8fe32647e8...7f75449765425d759565d3a770d829070d909f99 (the GitHub diff against main includes the prerequisite). ## Claims - Enable CUDA IPC for ModelOpt `FP8` and `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` linear layers using CUTLASS and the default format scheme. - Restore the transposed-weight layout metadata without transposing, requantizing, padding, or mutating the daemon's already processed weights/scales a second time. - Keep other ModelOpt FP8 backends and block FP8 unsupported; existing FP4/MXFP8 capability rules are unchanged. ## Validation Current head `7f75449765425d759565d3a770d829070d909f99` includes main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`. October 29 agent-run validation after resolving the inherited online-FP8 import conflict with upstream #60163. It adds no Humming IPC capability. | Check | Exact-head result | |---|---| | `modelopt-layers` | 117 passed, 5 deselected, 14 warnings in 85.71s (0:01:25) | | `modelopt-model` | 1 passed, 70 deselected, 18 warnings in 78.89s (0:01:18) | | Full feature-file and commit hooks | Passed, including mypy and ruff | Runtime: NVIDIA B300, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Encoder prefill attention on gfx1151: split-D head dims, alignment hint, launch config
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py` is the **encoder** attention kernel — ViT towers via the mm-encoder backend, the encoder branches of `TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN`, and `mimo_v2_omni`'s visual attention. (The paged LLM prefill path imports a same-named `context_attention_fwd` from `prefix_prefill.py`; that is a different module and is untouched here.)

It pads the head-dim tile to `next_power_of_2(head_dim)`, which wastes most of the matmul on the non-power-of-2 head dims vision towers use, and the KV tile #58225 picks for RDNA is still wider than those shapes want. On gfx1151 this is worth **2.19x** on the head_dim=72 kernel and takes Gemma3-4B's TTFT down **21%**.

Everything is inside one `if on_gfx1151()` in `context_attention_fwd` that only overrides launch values. Every other part keeps today's behaviour exactly: the launch arguments are computed as they are now, and only reassigned inside that branch.

```python
    BLOCK_DMODEL = triton.next_power_of_2(Lk)
    BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL = 0
    HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 = False

    if on_gfx1151() and q.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
        main = BLOCK_DMODEL // 2
        tail = max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(Lk - main))
        if Lk != BLOCK_DMODEL and main + tail < BLOCK_DMODEL:
            BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL = main, tail

        HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 = ...   # from the real strides of Q/K/V/O

        if HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 and (BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL) == (64, 16):
            BLOCK_N, num_warps = 16, 4
```

Exactly **one** existing line in the wrapper changes (`BLOCK_DMODEL=` in the launch). Four more change in `_fwd_kernel`, hoisting the head-axis offsets into locals so the alignment hint has something to annotate. Everything else is additive, and the new path is constexpr dead code when `BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL == 0`.

## Commits

| commit | what it does |
|---|---|
| `[ROCm] Split the head-dim block for non-power-of-2 head dims on gfx1151` | Covers the head dim as a power-of-2 main block plus a power-of-2 tail (72 → 64+16 = 80) behind a new constexpr `BLOCK_DMODEL_TAIL`; a tail of 0 reproduces the single-block kernel exactly. Skipped where it would not narrow the extent — 112 would be 64+64, the same 128 lanes for 12% more time. |
| `[ROCm] Narrow the KV tile for the 64 + 16 head dims on gfx1151` | Two things, and only one is about the tile. The `tl.multiple_of` hint on the head-axis offsets keeps the D-contiguous loads vectorized at `head_dim=72`, where the head stride is 8 mod 16 and Triton will not infer the alignment; it is set from the real strides and is unconditional. The narrow tile (`BLOCK_N=16`, 4 warps) is then taken only where that hint is active. |

## Performance

Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), against `upstream/main` which already includes #58225. Each pass checks out every point in turn and tables are the median of 3 such passes; spread is ±1% or better except where noted.

**Kernel** — `context_attention_fwd`, B=1, S=3520, H=16, bf16, non-causal, ms/call:

| head_dim | upstream | `+split` | `+narrow tile & hint` | total |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.727 | 1.745 (0.99x) | 1.741 (1.00x) | 0.99x |
| 72 | 4.842 | 2.524 (**1.92x**) | 2.213 (**1.14x**) | **2.19x** |
| 80 | 3.511 ±8% | 2.938 (**1.20x**) | 2.347 (**1.25x**) | **1.50x** |
| 96 | 3.578 | 3.222 (**1.11x**) | 3.230 (1.00x) | **1.11x** |
| 128 | 3.892 | 3.898 (1.00x) | 3.902 (1.00x) | 1.00x |
| 256 | 13.746 | 13.744 (1.00x) | 13.748 (1.00x) | 1.00x |

**The hint is unconditional; the tile is what depends on it.** At every head dim whose stride is already 16-byte aligned the hint is a tautology the compiler had anyway, and it measures exactly that. Each head dim on the tile it is given, median of 4 interleaved passes, ms/call:

| head_dim | no hint | with hint | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.814 | 1.813 | 1.00x |
| 72 | 2.887 | 2.302 | **1.25x** |
| 80 | 2.322 | 2.325 | 1.00x |
| 96 | 3.204 | 3.203 | 1.00x |
| 128 | 3.871 | 3.885 | 1.00x |
| 256 | 13.556 | 13.563 | 1.00x |

Only `head_dim=72`, the one that is 8 mod 16, learns anything from it. The narrow tile is the part that needs it: with vectorized loads `BLOCK_N=16` and 4 warps are worth 1.25x at both 72 (2.895 → 2.293) and 80 (2.924 → 2.331), but without them they are a regression — at `head_dim=72` with scalar loads the narrow tile runs 2.676 ms against 2.449 for the tile #58225 picks. Hence `if HEAD_STRIDE_ALIGNED_8 and ...`: a `head_dim` of 72 in a view whose head stride is padded keeps the wider tile.

**End to end** — TTFT, single 1920x1080 image, `max_tokens=1`, prefix caching and the multimodal processor cache disabled and a different image per repetition so every call really re-runs the vision tower. Median of 5, ms:

| model | ViT head_dim | upstream | `+split` | `+narrow tile & hint` | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `gemma-3-4b-it-quantized.w4a16` (SigLIP) | 72 | 442.8 | 362.2 (**−18.2%**) | 350.8 (−3.1%) | **−20.8%** |
| `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` | 80 | 1946.7 | 1934.4 (−0.6%) | 1907.1 (−1.4%) | **−2.0%** |

## Why these values

Against #58225's tile, median of 5 interleaved passes at S=3520:

| head_dim | split | #58225 tile | `BLOCK_N=16`, 4 warps | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | (64, 0) | 1.818 | 1.943 | 0.94x |
| 72 | (64, 16) | 2.909 | 2.309 | **1.26x** |
| 80 | (64, 16) | 2.934 | 2.341 | **1.25x** |
| 88 | (64, 32) | 3.202 | 3.350 | 0.96x |
| 96 | (64, 32) | 3.225 | 3.385 | 0.95x |
| 112 | (128, 0) | 3.672 | 8.009 | 0.46x |
| 128 | (128, 0) | 3.896 | 9.236 | 0.42x |

Hence the narrower tile is taken exactly for the 64 + 16 dims. No `waves_per_eu` override helped anywhere, so none is set, and `BLOCK_M` keeps the generic selection.

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_vit_prefill_attn.py` is added so this is reproducible; it launches `_fwd_kernel` directly so `--bm/--bn/--nw/--ns/--we` are honoured.

```
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_vit_prefill_attn.py --seq 3520 --heads 16 --head-dim 72 \
    --backend TRITON_ATTN --bm 128 --bn 16 --nw 4
```

## Testing

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_prefill_attention.py   128 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                            clean (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, SPDX)
```

The existing correctness tests only covered `head_dim` 128; they now also run 64, 72, 80 and 96, which between them exercise both tail widths the kernel can emit (72 and 80 split as 64+16, 96 as 64+32). 

## Not a duplicate

This builds on #58225, which caps `BLOCK_N` at 32 for all of RDNA3/RDNA4 and already covers head dims 96 and up on gfx1151 — which is why nothing is claimed there. What is left is the 64 + 16 dims, where the tile wants to be narrower still and the head dim needs the split in the first place.

#56232, #56253 and #56276 tune `triton_unified_attention.py` (decoder prefill/decode) — the same argument applied to the other attention kernel, no file overlap. Encoder attention reaches this kernel under both `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`, so #56232's backend reordering does not change whether this applies.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). Every line was reviewed by the submitter, and the measurements above were run and checked by hand.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kernel] New "hip" GDN backend for gfx1151
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

GATED_DELTA_NET prefill runs as a chain of Triton kernels that communicate through DDR. At 2048 tokens, 32 MiB are stored and loaded back per layer.

This adds the chunked delta rule (WY representation / UT transform) as a single HIP kernel for RDNA3.5. One block walks the chunks of one (head, sequence) with the state resident in registers and the per-chunk intermediates in LDS, so `h`, `w` and `u` are never formed. A chunk of 32 tokens and the identity `v_new = Tinv (V beta - (K beta exp(g_cs)) S)` keep a whole chunk inside the 64 KB LDS budget.

The kernel is also more accurate than the path it replaces: everything between the inputs and the output stays fp32, where the Triton kernels round `h`, `w`, `u`, `Tinv` and `v_new` to bf16. Against an fp64 token-by-token reference its relative RMS error is 0.53x theirs, and the final state comes out at fp32 precision.

The kernel is exposed as a new GDN prefill backend, `hip`, next to `triton`, `flashinfer`, `cutedsl` and `aiter_flydsl`:

- `auto` selects it on gfx1151, the only RDNA3.5 part run on hardware. Elsewhere `auto` keeps Triton.
- `--gdn-prefill-backend hip` enables it on gfx1150–gfx1153 and fails closed where the op is not built. `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` opts out.
- Built only for gfx1150–gfx1153. bf16 and fp16 Q/K/V/output and head dimension 128; other models resolve to Triton, and any call the kernel cannot serve falls back to Triton per call.
- The Triton/FLA path is untouched.

Also adds a single-GPU benchmark that compares the two paths correctness-first, with model presets, mixed-cache preparation and incremental JSONL output.

## Test Plan

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_chunked_rocm.py \
    tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py -v

# correctness against an fp64 token-by-token reference
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_chunk.py \
    --hv 48 --hg 16 --seqlens 32,33,64,1 --check --exact --raw-hip

# the timing grid below: four head shapes, 16 batches each
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_chunk.py --jsonl results.jsonl

# model-level accuracy
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --port 8765 --max-model-len 4096
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8765 \
    --num-questions 400 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0
```

<details>
<summary>What the benchmark does</summary>

**What it compares.** The Triton side calls the FLA entry point, `chunk_gated_delta_rule`; the HIP side calls the backend's wrapper, `chunk_gdn_hip_fwd`. Both are timed with their wrapper allocations, so the numbers are what each prefill backend costs per call.

**What it runs.** With no arguments it runs a fixed grid: 16 batches, from a single 32-token sequence up to 256 sequences of 256 tokens, against each of the four head shapes, which are the complete head counts of the Qwen3.5/3.6 family on one GPU. `--preset small|medium|dense|large` restricts the shapes. `--seqlens 941 --seqlens 1,4095` runs an explicit workload instead, repeatable, with `--hv`/`--hg` for its head counts and `--limit` to cut a run short. `--dtype` selects bf16 or fp16. `--dry-run` plans on CPU without importing torch, which is useful to see what a run would cover.

**How it times.** `triton.testing.do_bench` with quantiles, as elsewhere in this repository: it derives the repetition count from a first measurement and clears the L2 cache before each run, so every sample starts cold. Timing the public entry point means the samples include wrapper allocations and host launch gaps, which is what the model actually pays; `--raw-hip` additionally times the preallocated op on its own to separate that overhead from device time.

**What it checks before timing.** Output and final state are compared against the Triton path per sequence and head, with relative RMS and a finite check. `--check` skips timing entirely, and `--exact` adds an independent fp64 token-by-token recurrence, which is what decides whether the kernel is more accurate rather than merely different.

**Reading the output.** Progress goes to stdout; `--jsonl` writes one record per case with the median and the p10/p90 quantiles, the shapes, the inferred launch mode and the environment. Speedup is the Triton median over the HIP median, so above 1× is faster. Compare p10 and p90 before calling a small difference a regression: where those ranges overlap, the two paths are not conclusively different.

</details>

Hardware: one AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151). PyTorch `2.12.0+rocm10.1.0a20260803`, Triton `3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.1.0a20260803`. Only gfx1151 has been run on hardware; the other three targets are compile-tested.

## Test Result

`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_chunked_rocm.py`: **39 passed**. Coverage includes ratio-three heads, absent initial state, optional final state, continuation across aligned and unaligned splits, adversarial gates and fp16 inputs, all against an independent fp64 recurrence.

`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py`: **27 passed**. Covers backend selection (`auto` on and off gfx1151, explicit `hip`, unsupported head dims and dtypes, missing op) and, on gfx1151, the production `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` resolving to `hip` against a token-wise reference.

Every measured benchmark case passes its numerical checks.

| 16/16 | Qwen3.5-0.8B/2B | 16 | 2.19x | 0 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Raise the extensible KV cache margin floor to 3 GiB
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Raises the ROCm margin floor of the extensible KV cache (#56492) from 2 GiB to 3 GiB, so torch has enough room for memory fragmentation on MI355.

## Claims
 Fixes the OOMs in `(MI355) Spec Decode Eagle Nightly` ([ci#99485](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a039-403f-474a-9c3c-6c1ae7bc7fe5)) and `(MI355 DPX) Spec Decode Speculators + MTP` ([amd-ci#15764](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15764#01a1a0db-a987-452c-8c10-7a097faded05)).


## Validation

Tested on MI355X with the CI images. Without this PR, the Eagle and MiMo tests run out of memory when less memory is left for torch. With it, they pass, and the smallest headroom under the cap goes from 0.10 GiB to 0.67 GiB. The Eagle spec decode tests and the extensible KV cache unit tests give the same results with and without this PR.

To reproduce, run `test_eagle_correctness_medium[ROCM_AITER_FA-llama3_eagle3]` in the ci image with 100-200 MiB added to `KV_CACHE_NON_TORCH_RESERVE_BYTES`.

## Details

After warmup, vLLM limits how much memory torch can reserve. On ROCm, only about 1 GiB of that limit is left for fragmentation. The first large prefill of a 7-8B model leaves 1.3-1.7 GiB reserved but unused, so the next large allocation goes over the limit, even though the tensors in use would fit:

| Build | Limit | In use | Reserved, unused | Request |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ci#99485](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a039-403f-474a-9c3c-6c1ae7bc7fe5) | 18.84 GiB | 16.73 GiB | 1.27 GiB | 896 MiB |
| [amd-ci#15764](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15764#01a1a0db-a987-452c-8c10-7a097faded05) (DPX) | 18.93 GiB | 16.81 GiB | 1.70 GiB | 688 MiB |

The limit was added in #56492, and the spare room was small from the start: about 0.05-0.08 GiB, while fragmentation changes by 0.2-0.3 GiB from run to run.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Bugfix] wvSplitK: launch tiles of their own for gfx1151 and gfx1150; fix bigType for A_CHUNK 16
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Faster wave32 `wvSplitK` on gfx1151 and gfx1150/gfx1152/gfx1153: one launch tile per arch, chosen from a sweep of every non-spilling launch configuration. Related: #63015 (gfx9 rows only), #62718 (moves these kernels to a header; textual conflict), #51511 (disables the skinny GEMM on gfx1151; this PR makes it faster there instead). ## Claims - bf16/fp16 `wvSplitK` kernel time against `main`: +0.8% to +4.9% on gfx1150, +1.8% to +4.1% on gfx1151; 99.3-99.8% of the per-shape best tile (`main`: 96-98%). - Fixes `bigType` for A_CHUNK = 16 (64 B instead of 32 B: reads past the activation row, overlapping LDS writes). - GSM8K unchanged within noise. ## Validation **Performance.** Interleaved A/B against `main`, cold caches, weights padded as at load, median of 5 rounds. 43 shapes x N = 1..5, bf16 and fp16; 13 shapes not used for tuning (odd M, K = 768/1000/2880 among them); bias on 4 shapes. | | gfx1150 | gfx1151 | |---|---:|---:| | Shapes used for tuning | +1.8% to +1.9% | +2.7% to +3.0% | | Other shapes | +0.8% to +4.9% | +1.8% to +3.2% | | With bias | +1.7% | +4.1% | Cells slower by more than 2%: at most 3 of 150 per dtype, none below 0.98x. **Accuracy.** GSM8K, full set, 5-shot, greedy, a 1.5B bf16 instruct model, `max_num_seqs=5` (decode batches N = 1..5 through `wvSplitK`), gfx1151: | | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---:|---:| | `main` | 0.5807 ± 0.0136 | 0.5307 ± 0.0137 | | this PR | 0.5785 ± 0.0136 | 0.5292 ± 0.0137 | 3 and 2 of 1319 answers differ: the tile changes the summation order and `v_dot2_f32_bf16` the rounding. ``` lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct,dtype=bfloat16,max_num_seqs=5,max_model_len=4096,seed=0 \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --gen_kwargs temperature=0 --seed 0 ``` **Tests.** - `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_skinny_gemms.py -k test_rocm_wvsplitk_kernel`: 126 passed on gfx1151, including new K % 16 != 0 and N = 5 cases. The file's other failures on gfx1151 (`test_rocm_wvsplitk_fp8_kernel`, `test_rocm_llmm1_kernel`) are the same 184 on `main`. - All 43 shapes x N = 1..5, bf16/fp16, with and without bias, against `torch.nn.functional.linear`: correct on gfx1150 and gfx1151. - `pre-commit` passes. ## Details 1. **`bigType` sized by A_CHUNK.** `half4` was (A_CHUNK / 2) x bf16; it is now 4 x bf16, the operand of its only consumer. No launch used A_CHUNK = 16 before this PR. 2. **bf16 `DOT2C` on gfx11/gfx12** issues `v_dot2_f32_bf16`, as fp16 issues `v_dot2_f32_f16`, instead of widening both operands to f32. 3. **Launch rows** (`WVSPLITK_CFG_AC` takes A_CHUNK; `WVSPLITK_CFG` keeps 8): - gfx1151: (YTILE 1, UNRL 4, A_CHUNK 16); (2, 4, 8) for K < 1024. - gfx1150, gfx1152, gfx1153: (2, 1, 16); (1, 2, 16) when M <= 32 * CUs. - A_CHUNK 8 when K % 16 != 0 (wider chunks give wrong results there). - Other archs: unchanged. The sweep covered YTILE 1-4, UNRL 1/2/4/8, A_CHUNK 8/16/32 and WvPrGrp 16/32, excluding configurations that spill. AI assistance was used. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CI] Keep the chat template on NixlConnector PD + SD acceptance prompts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes `(MI355) NixlConnector PD + Spec Decode acceptance`, which has failed since [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245) landed ([amd-ci #15764](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15764#01a1a0db-a963-418a-a1cd-a003f97c4f00)). The test's MT-Bench prompts lost their chat template; dropping `backend="openai-chat"` from the `get_samples()` args restores it.

## Claims

- Test-only, one-line fix. The prompts are byte-identical to those before [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245).
- EAGLE3 acceptance length: 1.928 (FAIL, expected 2.600 ± 5%) → 2.583 (pass).
- No open PR addresses this failure: none touches this test or references [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245).

## Validation

CI job command, run on 2x MI355 in the failing build's image (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1a0d9-f1de-4511-92ce-35681c627064`), before and after the change:

```bash
cd /vllm-workspace/tests
KV_CACHE_MEMORY_BYTES=8G ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN \
  bash v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/config_sweep_spec_decode_test.sh
```

| Config | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAGLE3 Llama-3.1-8B, `kv_buffer_device=cuda` | 1.928 (FAIL) | 2.583 |
| EAGLE3 Llama-3.1-8B, `kv_buffer_device=cpu` | not reached | 2.583 |
| MTP Qwen3.5-0.8B, `kv_buffer_device=cuda` | not reached | 1.785 (expected 1.798) |

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

Before:
```
llama3-8b-eagle3: acceptance_length=1.928 (expected=2.600)
  Drafts: 10651, Accepted: 9884
E       AssertionError: Acceptance length regression for llama3-8b-eagle3! Expected: 2.600, Got: 1.928, Relative error: 25.85% (tolerance: 5%)
```

After:
```
llama3-8b-eagle3: acceptance_length=2.583 (expected=2.600)
  Drafts: 6663, Accepted: 10548
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 83.60s (0:01:23) ===================
llama3-8b-eagle3: acceptance_length=2.583 (expected=2.600)
  Drafts: 6663, Accepted: 10548
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 85.64s (0:01:25) ===================
qwen35-0.8b-mtp: acceptance_length=1.785 (expected=1.798)
  Drafts: 9428, Accepted: 7399
================== 1 passed, 16 warnings in 155.43s (0:02:35) ==================
✅ All spec decode acceptance tests passed!
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** [#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245) made `get_samples()` skip the client-side chat template for chat backends, since those endpoints apply it server-side. This test declares `backend="openai-chat"` but sends the prompts to `/v1/completions` with `add_special_tokens=False`. The prompts therefore reached the server with no chat template and no BOS, and acceptance dropped at every draft position. Without `backend`, the test builds its prompts the same way the standalone baseline in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py` does.

**Bisect.** Earlier nightlies consistently scored 2.603. The ROCm, PyTorch and Triton versions are identical between the passing and failing images. Overlaying each candidate commit's Python sources onto the last passing image (`5cdeea9`) gave `8b30f56` ([#65245](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65245)) as the first bad commit.

**Limitation.** With identical prompts, EAGLE3 scores 2.583 rather than 2.603. That shift is deterministic and comes from other engine changes that landed the same day. It is within tolerance, so the baseline is left unchanged.

AI assistance was used for the bisect, root-cause analysis, and this description. The submitter reviewed the change and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Use vllm.config.replace for the MRV1 DFlash draft config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

After #64096, MRV1 DFlash fails at engine startup. `DFlashProposer._create_draft_vllm_config` uses stdlib `dataclasses.replace` on `VllmConfig`. That passes the new `init=False` field `num_hash_lookahead_tokens` to the constructor, and Pydantic rejects it:

```
ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
num_hash_lookahead_tokens
  Unexpected keyword argument [type=unexpected_keyword_argument, input_value=0, input_type=int]
```

This PR uses `vllm.config.replace` instead. It skips `init=False` fields and is already used by the base proposer and the MRV2 DFlash loader. MRV2 is not affected.

## Validation

Fixes the nightly DFlash failures in [ci#99485](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485): AMD MI355 DPX shards [1/2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a04d-f648-41e8-9372-6ae84057341b) and [2/2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99485#01a1a053-720e-4b1d-8b8e-aee2981b06cf).

With this fix, both tests pass locally on MI355X:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_dflash_correctness[qwen3-mrv1]` | passed: GSM8K accuracy 0.884, acceptance length 4.12 |
| `test_dflash_reference_acceptance_lengths[False]` | passed: acceptance length mt-bench 4.12, humaneval 6.54, gsm8k 6.42 |
